S1. その上、S2. Means: on top of that; in addition (to that); what's more; besides; moreover その上 is used when the speaker wants to emphasize an additional piece of information. S2 usually contains the particle も or まで。 as here.
新型[しんがた]では ない ケータイを 使[つか]っているので、 ケータイで E メールが 出来[でき]ない。

{N/ANa/ANo} {である／であった／ではない／ではなかった} N である is the formal plain form of だ and can be affixed to nouns and -な／-の adjectives. である is used in formal writing. In very formal speech the polite form であります／ではありません may be used. である can occur before nouns in relative clauses while だ cannot.
ドラえもんは 実[じつ]は ネコ型[がた] ロボットなんです。

The preceding elements are mostly nouns, but some adjectival kanji characters can also precede 型(e.g. 大, 新, 薄). --- 英訳 [English translation]: style; type; pattern; make; model; design --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N + 型だ b. N1 + 型(の)N2
新型[しんがた]の インフルエンザの ワクチンは、 まだ ない そうだ。
I heard they don't have a vaccine for the new strain of influenza yet.

説明 [explanation]: 型 is a suffix meaning "style, type, model, etc." It is commonly used to describe the shape, type, model, or newness of an object. 次[つぎ]の 試合[しあい]は、 強[つよ]い チーム同士[どうし]の 戦[たたか]いに なるから、 どちらが 勝[か]つか 全[まった]く 分[わ]からない。

N同士 {が／で／を} Indicates that Ns do something together, that Ns do something to/for/against each other, or that someone puts Ns together in some way.
友達[ともだち]同士[どうし]で 話[はな]し合[あ]って 決[き]めて下[くだ]さい。
Please talk amongst your friends and make a decision.

N同士 {が／で／を} Indicates that Ns do something together, that Ns do something to/for/against each other, or that someone puts Ns together in some way.
「飲[の]むだけで やせられる 薬[くすり]」などと いう 広告[こうこく]は 信[しん]じない 方[ほう]が いいですよ。

V1-plain だけで V2 "just with ~; just by V-ing (is fine/enough/etc.) N/Vだけで is used to express the idea that X or just doing X is fine or good enough or that one can do something just with X or by doing X.

説明 [explanation]: The phrase literally means "if possible." It is also used when the speaker asks a favor of someone in a less direct way. できれば is slightly more formal than できたら. --- 英訳 [English translation]: if possible; if you don't mind; if it's all right --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ できれば／できたら
日本[にほん]では 外国[がいこく]人[じん]だと いう 理由[りゆう]で、 アパートを 貸[か]してもらえない ことが あるらしい。 信[しん]じられない。

S-plain という理由で "because" (lit. for the reason that~) is used to present the reason for a state, event, or action stated in the main clause. The phrase is usually used in written language.
今[こん]学期[がっき]は 日本[にほん]語[ご]や アジアの 歴史[れきし]などの クラスを 取[と]っています。

説明 [explanation]: など indicates that the given list is not exhaustive. When more than one item is listed, や is commonly used to connect the item. --- 英訳 [English translation]: N1やN2など = N1, N2 and others. N1やN2などのN3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. N1やN2など、N3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N1やN2など({は / も / が / を / に / の / etc.)} (N1 and N2 can be words or phrases).

説明 [explanation]: V-teくる and V-teいく indicate the temporal or spatial direction of an action from the speaker's viewpoint. V-teくる is used when an action appears to be directed toward the speaker, and V-teいく is used when it appears to be directed away from the speaker. V-teくる often indicates that an action or process began in the past and is continuing in the present, or that something has begun to take place. V-teいく, on the other hand, often expresses an action or state that will continue from the present into the future. In other uses, 来る and 行くfollowing V-te maintain their original meanings, i.e., "to come" and "to go." --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-teくる = have V-ed; begin to; become; grow V−teいく = go on V-ing; continue; become; grow --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te来る/行く

N + 型だ b. N1 + 型(の)N2

N という点から考えると "to view from the standpoint of ~; from the perspective of ~" used to indicate someone's view from the standpoint of X. Examples of X include business, environment, education, etc.

N {は／が／も} 少なくない "many; much; plenty of; not a few' 少なくない is a double negative meaning "many; much" and is commonly used in written language. It cannot modify nouns. For ex. 少なくない人 is a BAD expression.

説明 [explanation]: (1) This construction is used to state either a purpose or the way in which something is to be done. In XようにY, X represents a state or event which is beyond the control of the subject of Y. The verb form before ように is often a potential form or a negative form. (2) In the similar construction XためにY, X represents an action which can be controlled by the subject of Y, while XようにY implies that a certain consequence (X) will arise as the result of an action (Y). --- 英訳 [English translation]: so that ~; in such a way that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.nonpastように
A) ロボットが 作[つく]った 商品[しょうひん]を、 ここで 私[わたし]たち チェック するんです。 B） あー、 最後[さいご]に チェック するのは、 やっぱり 人間[にんげん]な わけですね。

~わけだ。 Means: The reason is that~; it means that~; that's why~; no wonder~; naturally Can be used in 3 situations, here it is (2) when a speaker reaches a logical conclusion based on what he/she has learned from the hearer or has discovered.

後のN "the remaining ~; the remainder of ~; the rest of ~" This use of 後 should be distinguished from 後 in the following example, where 後 means "~more." In this use, の cannot occur after 後. このプロジェクトには後三人必要だ。

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to describe X while indicating that X is not the only example, object, person, etc. --- 英訳 [English translation]: X is one of the ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ NはNPの{一つ/一人}だ。

N1 {では/じゃ}なく(て) N2 b. Phrase1 {では/じゃ}なく(て) Phrase2

説明 [explanation]: The particle ぐらい/くらい "approximately" often occurs with 同じ to mean "about the same." --- 英訳 [English translation]: about as ~ as; about the same ~ as ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N と同じ{ぐらい/くらい} b. N1 と同じ{ぐらい/くらい}の N2
私[わたし]の 国[くに]では 日本[にほん]に 旅行[りょこう]に 行[い]く 時[とき]、 旅行[りょこう] ビザを 取[と]る 必要[ひつよう]は ない。

説明 [explanation]: This phrase is used to indicate the necessity of doing something. は is common with a negative ending. --- 英訳 [English translation]: a. V必要がある = It is necessary to V; must V; have to V. b. V必要はない = It is not necessary to V; there is no need to V; don't have to V. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-past 必要{がある/はない}
私[わたし]は 来週[らいしゅう]、 学校[がっこう]の 代表[だいひょう]と して スピーチ コンテストに 出[で]ます。

説明 [explanation]: として is used to indicate the role, capacity, or occupation of someone or the function or characteristics of something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: as; in the capacity of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nとして1

説明 [explanation]: でしょう and だろう with rising intonation are used to elicit the hearer's confirmation. でしょう is the polite version of だろう. In casual conversation, male speakers use だろう and female speakers use でしょう. In more casual situations, the final う tends to drop. Note: でしょう and だろう with falling intonation indicate conjecture. --- 英訳 [English translation]: tag question(e.g. isn't it?; wasn't it?; aren't they?; is he?; are they?) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~だろう, ~でしょう
日本[にほん]の 有名[ゆうめい]な 小説[しょうせつ]が ハリウッドで 映画[えいが]化[か] される ことに なった。

説明 [explanation]: The suffix 化[か] is affixed to nouns and no-adjectives and adds the meaning of "-ization," as in "mechanization" and "digitization." --- 英訳 [English translation]: ～化する = ize; make; become; change to ～化する = ization; making ~; becoming ~; changing to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N + 化: 日本化; 専門化; 機械化 (mechanization); カタカナ化 b. NO-Adj + 化: 最適化 (optimization)
あの 映画[えいが]は 面白[おもしろ]い はずだよ。 映画[えいが] 先行[せんこう]の 友達[ともだち]が 3[さん]回[かい]も 見[み]たって 言[い]ってたから。

{V/A} -plain はず [seen here] ANa {な/じゃない/だった/じゃなかった) N {の/じゃない/だった/じゃなかった} "Should; I expect that ~; I believe that~" The dependent noun はず indicates that the speaker/writer or someone he/she empathizes with believes or expects that what is stated before はず is true based on his/her knowledge or memory at the moment of speech or at the time of the event stated in the main clause. The negative form can be either 〜ないはずだ or 〜はずがない.However, the sense of negation is stronger in はずがない. When Sはずだ modifies a noun, の must be used between はず and the noun.

{N/DemP} 以外に "Besides N/DemP" X以外に means "besides X" and に is sometimes omitted.

I've gotta go turn in my homework, so I'll turn yours in for you also, Mike.

In casual conversation contracted forms are commonly used.
私[わたし]の 大学[だいがく]の チームは 試合[しあい]に 出[で]る たびに、 負[ま]けてしまう。 もっと 強[つよ]くなってほしいなあ。

V-plain.non-past たびに "every time; each time; on every ~; whenever" たびに expresses the idea that each time someone does something, something else takes place. When たびに is modified by a noun, the noun refers to an action or certain time.
残念[ざんねん]な ことに、 私[わたし]達[たち]の チームは 最後[さいご]の 試合[しあい]で 負[ま]けてしまった。
Unfortunately, our team lost in the last match.

ANa なことに “It is~ that~; I am/We are ~ that ~; To my ~" ことに is used to express the speaker's feeling or subjective judgment about what is said in the main clause. ことに can only be used with a limited set of words.

N が第一 だ。 "first; first of all; to begin with; the first; the primary"
私[わたし]は 野球[やきゅう]を 見[み]るのが 好[す]きなんだけど、 トムさんは スポーツは 何[なに]が 好[す]き？
I like to watch baseball. What sports do you like, Tom?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: S んだけど／ですが is used as a preliminary remark by the speaker to inform the hearer of the speaker's desire, the current situation, etc. before (a) asking a question related to that desire, (b) asking for an opinion on the matter, or (c) making a request. This phrase can also be used to extend an invitation or an offer. When making a request, the request is often unstated, as shown below. んだけど is more casual than んですが. --- 英訳 [English translation]: but (in english, null in most situations) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜ん{だけど/ですが}

何より（も） "before everything; above all; first of all; more than anything else; the most ~"
私[わたし]は、 愛[あい]さえ あれば 幸[しあわ]せです。
As long as I have love, I am happy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Noun さえ with a verb conditional form is used when the condition presented in the clause is the only condition to make the statement in the main clause true. さえ replaces が and を in this structure; however, when other particles occur with さえ here, they do not drop. --- 英訳 [English translation]: If~ only ~; If~ just ~; as long as; --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N( = clause X) さえ V-cond (= clause Y)
私[わたし]の 友達[ともだち]は、 フランスで ファッション モデルと して 働[はたら]いています。
My friend works in France as a fashion model.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: として is used to indicate the role, capacity, or occupation of someone or the function or characteristics of something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: as; in the capacity of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nとして
私[わたし]は 旅行[りょこう]が 大好[だいす]きで 世界[せかい]中[じゅう]を 旅行[りょこう] した。 南極[なんきょく] （へ/に）さえ 行[い]った ことが ある。
I love traveling and I've traveled all over the world. I've even been to Antarctica.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (prt) さえ Means: even さえ is an emphatic particle. In non-conditional clauses it means "even." When さえ is used, the particle が never occurs, を usually does not occur, へ and the directional に are optional, and the other particles, including the LOCATIONAL に, で、と and から are mandatory.
私[わたし]は 日本[にほん] 文学[ぶんがく]を 研究[けんきゅう] したいと 思[おも]っている。だが、 両親[りょうしん]は 私[わたし]に 医者[いしゃ]に なってほしがっている。

S1. だが、S2. "but; however" だが is a disjunctive conjunction. S1 and S2 present contrastive statements or opposing ideas. Note: でも、けれど、けど are colloquial けれども、しかしながら、だが、and が are primarily used in written language. しかし can be used in both written and spoken language.
両親[りょうしん]は 私[わたし]に、 いつも 早[はや]く 家[いえ]に 帰[かえ]ってくる ように 言[い]います。

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
家[いえ]に 帰[かえ]って、 まず 最初[さいしょ]に する ことは、 手[て]を 洗[あら]って うがい (gargle)を する ことです。
The first thing I do when I get home is wash my hands and gargle.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
説明 [explanation]: まず is an adverb meaning "first of all." --- 英訳 [English translation]: first of all; first; to begin with; before everything
週末[しゅうまつ]は、 勉強[べんきょう] 以外[いがい]に、 テニスを したり 映画[えいが]を 見[み]たり します。
Besides studying, I do things like play tennis and watch movies on the weekend.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{N/DemP} 以外に "Besides N/DemP" X以外に means "besides X" and に is sometimes omitted.
私[わたし]が 住[す]んでいる アパートは、 周[まわ]りが 静[しず]かなだけでなく 安全[あんぜん]でも あるので、 学生[がくせい]に 人気[にんき]が ある。
The apartment I'm living in is in an area that's not just quiet; it's also safe, so it's popular among students.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N／ANa でもある "be also" X は Y でもある. OR X は Y でもあり、Z でもある。 Are used to introduce another property of X when X has more than one property.
田中[たなか] 先生[せんせい]の 研究[けんきゅう]室[しつ]には、 百[ひゃく]年[ねん] 以上[いじょう] 前[まえ]の 辞書[じしょ]も あれば、 最近[さいきん]の 映画[えいが]の DVDも ある。
In Professor Tanaka's office there are dictionaries from more than a hundred years ago as well as DVDs of recent films.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1も V-conditional, N2 も V。 Means: some do ~ and others do ~; do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; there are times when ~ and times when ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well. This sentence structure is used to present some members in a group, things in a category, actions someone takes, characteristics of something/someone, etc. among others. Although the form of the verb here is conditional, the meaning is NOT conditional in its usage.
私[わたし]は よく 両親[りょうしん]に 弟[おとうと]を いじめない ように 言[い]われます。
My parents often tell me not to tease my little brother. (Indirect Quote)
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
私[わたし]は この 教科[きょうか]書[しょ]が 大好[だいす]きだ。 何[なに]より、 単語[たんご]と 漢字[かんじ]が 覚[おぼ]えやすいと いうのが いい。
I love this textbook. More than anything else, the way it makes it easy to remember vocabulary and kanji is good.

何より（も） "before everything; above all; first of all; more than anything else; the most ~"
私[わたし]は 毎日[まいにち] 漢字[かんじ]を 五つ[いつつ]ずつ 覚[おぼ]える ことに している。
I make it a rule to memorize five kanji a day.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{Number +(counter)} +ずつ "per/a; at a time; each; (little) by (little)" The number/amount X+ずつ indicates that someone does something (or something happens) with X as the unit.
両親[りょうしん]は 毎日[まいにち]の ように、 よく 勉強[べんきょう] していい 大学[だいがく]に 入[はい]りなさいと 言[い]います。 それなら、 私[わたし]が 勉強[べんきょう] している とき、 弟[おとうと]や 妹[いもうと]に 静[しず]かにする ように 言[い]ってほしいと 思[おも]います。
My parents tell me almost every day to study hard so I can get into a good university. If that's what they want, I want them to tell my little brother and sister to be quiet while I'm studying.

それなら "If that's the case; If so" それ meaning "that" refers to the speaker's previous statement of the statement which was just made by the hearer.
私[わたし]の 家[いえ]では 食事[しょくじ]の 後[あと]、 自分[じぶん]が つかった お皿[さら]を 洗[あら]う ことに なっている。
At my house, the rule is that you wash your own place after a meal.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.non-past ことになっている means that something has been decided and the result of the decision is still in effect. It is often used to introduce rules or customs, as well as one's schedule. --- 英訳 [English translation]: be supposed to ~; It is a rule that ~; It's been decided that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-past ことになっている: {行く/行かない}ことになっている
今週[こんしゅう]中[ちゅう]に メールを 出[だ]すか 電話[でんわ]を 掛[か]けるか しますから、 待[ま]っていて下[くだ]さい。
I'll either e-mail you or call you some time this week, so please wait for that.

説明 [explanation]: The phrase AかBか is used to present alternatives. When Bか is followed by a case particle (e.g., が, を, へ, に, で, と), the second か is usually dropped. --- 英訳 [English translation]: either A or B; whether A or B --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. 〜か〜か b. N1かN2+Particle
日本[にほん]語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]になる 地[ち] つれて、 日本[にほん]人[じん]と 話[はな]すのが 静[しずか] 香[かぐわ]しくなくなってきた。
As my Japanese improves, I've become less embarrassed when talking with Japanese people.

V-non-past.aff につれて "as ~; with ~" Xにつれて indicates that omething takes place as X occurs. X can be either a verb or the stem of a suru-V.
最近[さいきん]、 日本[にほん]でも 現金[げんきん]の 代[か]わりに カードを 使[つか]う 人[ひと]が 多[おお]くなった。
Recently, many people have begun using cards in place of cash in Japan, too.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: の代わりに is used to present something/someone that is replacing or has replaced something/someone. When the context is clear, Noun の can be omitted. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in place of; instead of; to make up for --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nの代わりに
この 車[くるま]は 機能[きのう]性[せい]と 同時[どうじ]に 安全[あんぜん]性[せい]に ついても よく 考[かんが]えて 作[つく]られている。
This car was designed with both functionality and safety in mind.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
VN/Nと同時に "as soon as; the moment; at the same time; also; as well"
現代[げんだい]人[じん]に とって、 コンピュータの ない 生活[せいかつ]は 考[かんが]えられないだろう。
I feel that life without computers is unthinkable to people today.

N {は／なんて} 考えられない "unimaginable; inconceivable; unthinkable"
この 情報[じょうほう]を 見[み]るには、 この ソフトウェアを インストール する 必要[ひつよう]が あります。
In order to view this information, it is necessary to install this software.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past.aff には "to; in order to; for; for the purpose of; when" には indicates purpose in general statements (often stating the speaker's judgement about an action in terms of its effectiveness, convenience, necessity, etc.). には can also mean "when" (=時には). Verbs or nouns can precede には. Note that when ために is used, the predicate in the main clause describes an action. Such that: Xには Y, where Y is a judgment and never an action XためにY, where Y is an action and never a judgement. AND, XためにはY, where Y is a judgment, never an action
この プロジェクトは、 社長[しゃちょう]の 考[かんが]え 次第[しだい]で 変[か]わる 可能[かのう]性[せい]が ある。

N次第で "depending on N" When 次第 is affixed to nouns, it means "depend on."
この 問題[もんだい]を いかに 解決[かいけつ] すべきか、 みんなで 話[はな]し合[あ]わなくては ならない。
We all need to discuss how we should solve this problem.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
いかに〜か "how; how much; in what way" This structure occurs as an embedded interrogative sentence, where いかに means "how (much)" or "in what way". This structure is commonly used in written language.
ウィキペディアの こと 人物[じんぶつ]に 関[かん]する 情報[じょうほう]は 正[ただ]しくない ようだ。
It seems that the information Wikipedia has on this person is incorrect.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 に関する N2 formal "with regard to; concerning; regarding; about; on; related to"
だいたいの 数[かず]は 分[わ]かりますが、 正確[せいかく]な 数[かず]は 調[しら]べてみないと 分[わ]かりません。
We have approximate figures, but we'll have to do some research to get an accurate count.

だいたい number/amount "approximately number/amount" だいたい means "most;almost; nearly(all); approximate." The meaning changes depending on what だいたい modifies.
インタ ネットを 通[とお]して、 色々[いろいろ]な 情報[じょうほう]を 得[え]る ことが 出来[でき]る。
You can get all sorts of information over the Internet.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N を通して "through; via" を通して indicates a medium (X) through which someone does something or something happens. X can be things, people, activities or actions.
作文[さくぶん]は ワープロで 書[か]いても いい はずだが、 一応[いちおう]、 先生[せんせい]に 聞[き]いてみよう。
It should be fine to use a word processor to write the composition, but let's ask the teacher, just in case.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

一応 "for the time being; for now; tentatively; although not perfectly; sort of; just in case" In this sentence the use means "tentatively" 一応 is used when an action/state is tentative or not quite complete, perfect or satisfactory. It is also used when an action is taken as a precaution.
オリンピックを する ことに 決[き]まってから、 その 国[くに]は 国際[こくさい]的[てき]になってきた。
After it was decided that it would host the Olympics, that country has become more cosmopolitan.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N+的 the suffix is attached to nouns to make them な-adjectives. When these adj modify nouns, the な is sometimes omitted.
東京[とうきょう]の 物価[ぶっか]は ニューヨークと 同[おな]じぐらい 高[たか]い。

説明 [explanation]: The particle ぐらい/くらい "approximately" often occurs with 同じ to mean "about the same." --- 英訳 [English translation]: about as ~ as; about the same ~ as ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N と同じ{ぐらい/くらい} b. N1 と同じ{ぐらい/くらい}の N2
東京[とうきょう]は 人[ひと]が 多[おお]い 上[うえ]に、 物価[ぶっか]が 高[たか]い。だから、 住[す]みにくい。
Tokyo's not just crowded, it's also expensive. That makes it a hard place to live.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S 上に "in addition to~; besides~; not only~but also~; moreover~; ~ as well" The conjunction 上に introduces additional information emphatically.
本当[ほんとう]である 限[かぎ]り 本当[ほんとう]でない 限[かぎ]り
As long as it's true... As long as it isn't true...
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ANoで {ある／ない} V-plain 限り "as long as; as far as; while; until; unless; as much as; as much as (one can)" this grammar is used when something is the case or is true as long as the condition in X holds true. It is also used to indicate the extent to which one can do something or one knows something. (as far as one can; as far as one knows)
日本[にほん]語[ご]の 先生[せんせい]が いつも 日本[にほん]人[じん]だとは 限[かぎ]らない。 とても いい 外国[がいこく]人[じん]の 先生[せんせい]も たくさん いる。
Not all Japanese teachers are Japanese. There are a lot of excellent non-native teachers, too.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
〜とは限らない "not necessarily~; not always ~; it's not necessarily the case that~" Xとは限らない means "it's not necessarily the case that X." だ before とは is optional.
高[たか]い レストランだから おいしいとは 限[かぎ]らない。
It's not always true that expensive restaurants serve good food.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
〜とは限らない "not necessarily~; not always ~; it's not necessarily the case that~" Xとは限らない means "it's not necessarily the case that X." だ before とは is optional.
プレイスメント テストに 合格[ごうかく] しない 限[かぎ]り、 上[うえ]の レベルの クラスには 入[い]れません。
You won't be able to take upper-level classes until you pass the placement test.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain 限り "as long as; as far as; while; until; unless; as much as; as much as (one can)" this grammar is used when something is the case or is true as long as the condition in X holds true. It is also used to indicate the extent to which one can do something or one knows something. (as far as one can; as far as one knows)
サッカーの 面白[おもしろ]さは テレビで 見[み]ているだけでは 分[わ]からない。 スタジアムに 行[い]って 実際[じっさい]に 見[み]てこそ 本当[ほんとう]の 面白[おもしろ]さが 分[わ]かるのだ。
You can't understand how interesting soccer is just from watching it on TV. It's only when you go to a stadium and watch it in person that you can really understand its appeal.

V-te こそ "the very ~; It is that~; in particular; precisely; definitely; only (when, by doing, etc~)" こそ emphasizes the preceding word, phrase or clause. When こそ is used, the particles は、が and を drop.
指示[しじ] 通[どお]りに、 ここに 答[こた]えを 書[か]いて下[くだ]さい。

Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N通り（に） Where 通り is a suffix and reads as どおり。 "the way; as; exactly like; following; according to" When 通り is modified by a verb or noun, it means "the way; as someone does; as something indicates." 通り can also be used as a suffix, in which case 通り is directly affixed to nouns and the pronunciation changes from とおり to どおり。
教育[きょういく]の 平等[びょうどう]と いう 点[てん]から 考[かんが]えると、 現在[げんざい]の 教育[きょういく] 制度[せいど]には 問題[もんだい]が ある。
From the point of view of equality in education, there are problems with the current educational system.

N という点から考えると "to view from the standpoint of ~; from the perspective of ~" used to indicate someone's view from the standpoint of X. Examples of X include business, environment, education, etc.
この 大学[だいがく]は 外国[がいこく]人[じん]が 多[おお]くて、 国際[こくさい]化[か]が 進[すす]んでいる。

N＋化 Meaning: -ization; making ~; becoming~; changing to ~ The suffix 化 adds the meaning "-ization" to nouns and no-adjectives.説明 [explanation]: The suffix 化[か] is affixed to nouns and no-adjectives and adds the meaning of "-ization," as in "mechanization" and "digitization." --- 英訳 [English translation]: ～化する = ize; make; become; change to ～化する = ization; making ~; becoming ~; changing to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N + 化: 日本化; 専門化; 機械化 (mechanization); カタカナ化 b. NO-Adj + 化: 最適化 (optimization)
この 製品[せいひん]に 使[つか]われている ものは、 何[なに]から 何[なに]まで リサイクル できます。

何から何まで "all; anything and everything; all kinds" 何から何まで means "all" and is more emphatic than 全部, すべて、or みんな. 何から何まで can be used with 全部、みんな、and すべて。
この 本[ほん]は、 話[はな]し言葉[ことば]的[てき] 表現[ひょうげん]で 書[か]かれているので、 とても 分[わ]かりやすい。
This book is written in a colloquial style, so it's very easy to understand.

N+的 the suffix is attached to nouns to make them な-adjectives. When these adj modify nouns, the な is sometimes omitted.

結構 (A/ANa +だ) Means: fairly; pretty; rather; quite The adverb 結構 indicates that the speaker feels that the degree/level/amount/etc. of something is not high, but is higher than average
会議[かいぎ]が 始[はじ]まってから もう 3[さん]時間[じかん] 以上[いじょう] 経[た]っている。 いったい いつ 終[お]わるのだろうか。

いったい QW "(what, who, where, how, etc.) on earth" いったい is an intensifier used with questions. It usually occurs immediately preceding the question word, but it may appear in other locations before the QW.
コンピュータが フリーズ する 問題[もんだい]は 一応[いちおう] 解決[かいけつ] したけれど、 まだ、 メールが 文字[もじ] 化[ば]け すると いう 問題[もんだい]が 残[のこ]っている。

一応 "for the time being; for now; tentatively; although not perfectly; sort of; just in case" In this sentence the use means "tentatively" 一応 is used when an action/state is tentative or not quite complete, perfect or satisfactory. It is also used when an action is taken as a precaution.
技術[ぎじゅつ]が 発達[はったつ] した ために、 生活[せいかつ]が とても 便利[べんり]になってきた。

説明 [explanation]: V-teくる and V-teいく indicate the temporal or spatial direction of an action from the speaker's viewpoint. V-teくる is used when an action appears to be directed toward the speaker, and V-teいく is used when it appears to be directed away from the speaker. V-teくる often indicates that an action or process began in the past and is continuing in the present, or that something has begun to take place. V-teいく, on the other hand, often expresses an action or state that will continue from the present into the future. In other uses, 来る and 行くfollowing V-te maintain their original meanings, i.e., "to come" and "to go." --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-teくる = have V-ed; begin to; become; grow V−teいく = go on V-ing; continue; become; grow --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te来る/行く
B型[がた]の 性格[せいかく]は 楽天[らくてん]なのに 対[たい]して、 A型[がた]は まじめな 性格[せいかく]だと 言[い]われている。
It is said that people with blood type B are optimistic, whereas people with blood type A are serious.

Sのに対して "whereas; on the other hand; in contrast" に対して is used when contrasting two actions, states, situations, etc.
この 公園[こうえん]は 地図[ちず]の 上[うえ]では 家[いえ]から 近[ちか]い ように 見[み]えるが、 歩[ある]くと 結構[けっこう] 時間[じかん]が かかる。
On a map this park looks close to the house, but when you walk there it takes quite a while.

N のうえで "in terms of; from the viewpoint of ~; as far as ~ is concerned; according to ~" Nの上で and N上 are used to indicate that the speaker's statement refers only to N. Commonly used in written language.
まだ 反[はん]しあわなくては いけない 問題[もんだい]が ありますが、 時間[じかん]に なりましたので、 今日[きょう]は、 一応[いちおう]、 これで 会議[かいぎ]を 終[お]わります。
There are still problems we need to discuss, but we're out of time, so we'll end the meeting here for now.

一応 "for the time being; for now; tentatively; although not perfectly; sort of; just in case" In this sentence the use means "tentatively" 一応 is used when an action/state is tentative or not quite complete, perfect or satisfactory. It is also used when an action is taken as a precaution.
ゆうべ 飲[の]み過[す]ぎた せいで、 朝[あさ]から 頭[あたま]が ガンガン する。
I drank too much alst night, so my head has been throbbing since this morning.

{V/A}-plain せい "because; due to" Both おかげ and せい are dependent nouns indicating cause. The former is used when the cause brings about a desirable result, and the latter when the cause brings about an unwanted result.
上手[じょうず]な 選手[せんしゅ]が いなくても、 負[ま]けるとは 限[かぎ]らない。 チームワークで 勝[か]てる ことも ある。
Even if you don't have a strong player, it doesn't necessarily mean you'll lose. There are cases where teamwork wins games.

〜とは限らない "not necessarily~; not always ~; it's not necessarily the case that~" Xとは限らない means "it's not necessarily the case that X." だ before とは is optional.
ハイブリッドの 車[くるま]が 増[ふ]えた ことに よって、 町[まち]の 空気[くうき]が きれい なってきました。
Because hybrid cars increased, the city's air came to be cleaner.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
~ことによって によって indicates the cause, the means, or the agent in passive sentences. In this sentence it indicates CAUSE. "because; because of; due to; by V-ing; by means of; via; through; by"
外国[がいこく] 語[ご]は 話[はな]せば 話[はな]すほど、 上手[じょうず]になります。 そして、 読[よ]めば 読[よ]むほど、 単語[たんご]が 増[ふ]えます。
The more you speak a foreign language, the more skilled you become. In addition, the more you read, the more your vocabulary increases.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-cond {V/A}-plain ほど "the (more) ~, the (more) ~" This structure is used when the more something happens or is in some state, the more another thing happens or is in some state. (When V is a suru verb, the second VN is usually omitted)
「とびら」 サイトを 利用[りよう] する 人[ひと]が 毎日[まいにち] 少[すこ]しずつ 増[ふ]えている。

Grammar,扉,Intermediate
non-specific amount expression + ずつ "per/a; at a time; each; (little) by (little)" The number/amount X+ずつ indicates that someone does something (or something happens) with X as the unit.
レポートは 一応[いちおう] 書[か]き上[あ]げたけれど、 英語[えいご]の スペル チェックが まだだ。
I've sort of finished the report (although not perfectly), but I still need to do an English spell check.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

一応 "for the time being; for now; tentatively; although not perfectly; sort of; just in case" In this sentence the use means "although not perfectly" 一応 is used when an action/state is tentative or not quite complete, perfect or satisfactory. It is also used when an action is taken as a precaution.
病気[びょうき]の 人[ひと]に 言[い]う 「 お大事[だいじ]に」と いう 表現[ひょうげん]は、 英語[えいご]で 言[い]うと” Please take care."に 当[あ]たります。
The expressions "O-daijini" which is said to sick people, corresponds to the English "Please take care".
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

"in terms of; in; according to; from the viewpoint of" で言うと is used to restate something according to a different system or framework (e.g. a calendar, a measurement system, a language, a country's history)
この ノートに 書[か]いてある ことは 全部[ぜんぶ] 覚[おぼ]えたと 思[おも]うが、 一応[いちおう]、 もう 一度[いちど] 見[み]ておこう。
I think I've mmemorized everything written in this notebook, but I'll take another look, just in case.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

一応 "for the time being; for now; tentatively; although not perfectly; sort of; just in case" In this sentence the use means "tentatively" 一応 is used when an action/state is tentative or not quite complete, perfect or satisfactory. It is also used when an action is taken as a precaution.
パーティの 準備[じゅんび]は 一応[いちおう] 終[お]わった。 後[あと]は 飲[の]み物[もの]を 出[だ]すだけだ。
I've pretty much finished with the party prep. All that's left is to put out the drinks.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

一応 "for the time being; for now; tentatively; although not perfectly; sort of; just in case" In this sentence the use means "tentatively" 一応 is used when an action/state is tentative or not quite complete, perfect or satisfactory. It is also used when an action is taken as a precaution.
富士[ふじ]山[やま]の 高[たか]さは 何[なん]キロくらいでしょうか。
About how many kilometers is the height of Mt. Fuji, I wonder.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The suffix さ is attached to the stem of an i-adjective or a na-adjective to form a noun. The typical effect is the addition of this suffix "-ness," as in "niceness" or "-ty," as in "rarity." --- 英訳 [English translation]: -ness; -ty --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {A-stem / ANa} + さ: ひろい + さ = ひろさ; さむい + さ = さむさ; 元気さ; 便利さ; (Exception: いい = よさ)
世界[せかい]で 一番[いちばん] 長[なが]い 川[かわ]は ナイルだと 言[い]われているが、 アマゾン川[かわ]だと 言[い]う 人[ひと]も 居[い]る。

Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to introduce something commonly said about something or someone. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~ it is said to be ~, It is said that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ーはSentence-plainと言われている
天気[てんき] 予報[よほう]は、 今日[きょう]は 雨[あめ]だと 言[い]っていた。 ところが、 とても いい 天気[てんき]に なった。
The weather forecast said that it would rain today, but we ended up having beautiful weather.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ところが is a sentence initial conjunction used when something takes place which is unexpected from the preceding context. The sentence after ところが represents an event or action the speaker cannot control. --- 英訳 [English translation]: however; but; nevertheless --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S１。ところが S２ where S1=what's expected; S2= what actually occurred.
示教[しきょう]に 熱心[ねっしん]な 信者[しんじゃ]は、 示教[しきょう] 活動[かつどう]を 中心[ちゅうしん]に 生活[せいかつ]を している。
The most fervent followers of religions center their lives around religious activities.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N を 中心 {と/に} (して） "(centering) around; focusing on; mainly; with N as the center/focus/leader/etc." Nを中心(と/に)する literally means "to make N the center." This phrase takes 2 forms. The form used here is used to modify verbs. The phrase indicates that something takes place around N or with N as the center/focus, or that someone does something focusing on N.
病状[びょうじょう]に 合[あ]わせて、 いろいろな 薬[くすり]が 使[つか]われる。
A variety of medicines are used depending on the condition of the patient.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N に会わせて "making ~ suitable for N; according to N" The literal meaning this grammar is "fitting/matching/adjusting something to N" and is often used to mean "making something suitable for N" or "according to N"
両親[りょうしん]や 先生[せんせい]が いつも 正[ただ]しいとは 限[かぎ]らないが、 一応[いちおう]、 アドバイスは もらっておいた 方[ほう]が いい。
Parents and teachers aren't always right, but it's a good idea to get their advice anyways, just in case.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
〜とは限らない "not necessarily~; not always ~; it's not necessarily the case that~" Xとは限らない means "it's not necessarily the case that X." だ before とは is optional.
この 大学[だいがく]の 学生[がくせい]である 限[かぎ]り、 大学[だいがく]が 決[き]めた ルールは 守[まも]らなくては いけません。
As long as you're a student here, you have to abide by the university's rules.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain 限り "as long as; as far as; while; until; unless; as much as; as much as (one can)" this grammar is used when something is the case or is true as long as the condition in X holds true. It is also used to indicate the extent to which one can do something or one knows something. (as far as one can; as far as one knows)
天気[てんき]に 気分[きぶん]を 左右[さゆう] される 人[ひと]は、 結構[けっこう] 多[おお]い。
There are quite a few people whose moods are influenced by the weather.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 を N2 左右する "influence; govern" 左右する is most commonly used in written language.
最近[さいきん]の ケータイは 複雑[ふくざつ] 過[す]ぎて、 便利[べんり]か 便利[べんり]じゃないか 分[わ]からない。
Cell phones these days are so complicated that it's hard to say whether or not they are really useful.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The phrase AかBか is used to present alternatives. When Bか is followed by a case particle (e.g., が, を, へ, に, で, と), the second か is usually dropped. --- 英訳 [English translation]: either A or B; whether A or B --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. 〜か〜か b. N1かN2+Particle
レオナルド・ ダ・ビンチは 芸術[げいじゅつ]家[か]でも あり、 科学[かがく]者[しゃ]でも あった。
Leonardo da Vinci was a scientiest as well as an artist.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N／ANa でもある "be also" X は Y でもある. OR X は Y でもあり、Z でもある。 Are used to introduce another property of X when X has more than one property.
この 留学[りゅうがく] プログラムは、 ホームステイが できると いう 点[てん]が、 セールス ポイントですね。
The fact that this study abroad program provides students with the opportunity to do a homestay is one of its selling points, isn't it?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N {という/の} 点で (は） "in terms of ~; with regard to ~; with respect to ~" 点 is used to mean "point" (in the sense of a single, fact, idea or opinion in an argument, discussion, etc.), "aspect," or "viewpoint/standpoint."
日本[にほん]に 留学[りゅうがく] した 経験[けいけん]を 生[い]かして、 大学[だいがく]の 留学[りゅうがく] アドバイザーに なる つもりだ。
I intend to make the most of my experience studying abroad in Japan and become a study-abroad adviser at a university.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
生かす "make the most of; make the best use of; use effectively; maintain" 生かす means literally "to keep alive," but it is also used to mean "to make the most of one's ability, etc"
この 大学[だいがく]には、 外国[がいこく]から きている 留学[りゅうがく]生[せい]も 少[すく]なくない そうだ。
I hear that there are also a considerable amount of foreign students at this university.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N {は／が／も} 少なくない "many; much; plenty of; not a few' 少なくない is a double negative meaning "many; much" and is commonly used in written language. It cannot modify nouns. For ex. 少なくない人 is a BAD expression.
今[いま]、 どこの 大学[だいがく]に 留学[りゅうがく] してたっけ？
Where is the University that you are studied abroad at now?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{V/A}-plain.past (んだ）っけ っけ is a question marker used in very casual conversation. Note that after the non-past forms of V, A and ~ない, んだ must be used before っけ。
マイクさん、 今[いま]、 どこの 大学[だいがく]に 留学[りゅうがく] してたっけ？
(I forget…) What was the name of the university where Mike's doing his study abroad?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{V/A}-plain.past (んだ）っけ っけ is a question marker used in very casual conversation. Note that after the non-past forms of V, A and ~ない, んだ must be used before っけ。
日本[にほん]に 留学[りゅうがく]中[ちゅう]は、 ホームステイの 家族[かぞく]を はじめ 色々[いろいろ]な 人[ひと]に お世話[せわ]に なった。
When I was studying in Japan, a lot of people helped me out, starting with my host family.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Noun をはじめ is used to present a primary example when mentioning a group of things or people. --- 英訳 [English translation]: beginning with~; starting with ~; including ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nをはじめ
日本[にほん]に 留学[りゅうがく] したいと 思[おも]う 一方[いっぽう]、 外国[がいこく]に 住[す]む ことに 不安[ふあん]も ある。

S1 一方（で）、S2. "While; when; at the same time; on the other hand" The conjunction 一方 is used to present two contrastive situations or two concurrent states, events or actions. 一方 is usually used in written language.
今年[ことし]こそ 日本[にほん]に 留学[りゅうがく] したいと 思[おも]っている。
I really want to go to Japan to study this year.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N こそ "the very ~; It is that~; in particular; precisely; definitely; only (when, by doing, etc~)" こそ emphasizes the preceding word, phrase or clause. When こそ is used, the particles は、が and を drop.
留学[りゅうがく] すると いうのは、 外国[がいこく]で 勉強[べんきょう] すると いう ことだ。
Ryuugakusuru means to study in a foreign country.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The structure ~というのは~だ is used to provide the meaning or definition of a word or phrase. --- 英訳 [English translation]: X means ~; The meaning of X is ~; What X means is ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. ~ というのは {Nのこと / N ということ}だ b. ~ というのは Sことだ. Type 2c c. ~ というのは {Sということ/Sという意味}だ. Type 1
今日[きょう]は 授業[じゅぎょう]に 出[で]る ほかは、 何[なに]も 予定[よてい]が ない。
Aside from attending the class, I don't have any plans today.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Nの他に(も) is an adverbial phrase meaning "in addition to N." Verbs, adjectives and demonstrative adjectives can also precede 他に(も) to mean "in addition to V-ing," "in addition to being Adj." or "in addition to this/that." ~他(に)は also means "in addition to." In some contexts, the phrase can mean "except for; other than" --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~他に(も) = in addition to ~; besides ~他(に)は(~ない) = (not ~) except for ~; (not~) other than ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~他に(も); ~他(に)は {この/その/あの}他に(も)
授業[じゅぎょう]に 関係[かんけい]の ない 質問[しつもん]は しない ようにしましょう。
Try not to ask questions that are not related to the lesson.

N1 {と/に} 関係 {が/の} あるN2. This sentence is used to show that N1 is related in someway to N2. The particle after N1 may be と or に。 When this pattern is used in relative clauses, の is commonly used after 関係 instead of が。
なんだ、 まだ 宿題[しゅくだい] 終[お]わってないの。 早[はや]くしないと、 授業[じゅぎょう]が はじまっちゃうよ。
Oh, you're not done with your homework yet? Hurry up; class is about to start.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
なんだ "oh!" The literal meaning of なんだ is "What is X?" However it can also be used to express the speaker's slight surprise。 Used only in very casual conversation.
来年[らいねん]は、 少[すく]なくとも 3[みっ]つは 授業[じゅぎょう]を 取[と]らなければいけない。
Next year, I have to take at least three classes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
少なくとも N (は） 少なくとも means "at least." It can be used with a noun or number. When used with a noun, は often follows the noun (or the particle after the noun), indicating that the noun is under focus.
登録[とうろく] した 学生[がくせい]が 少[すく]ないと いう 理由[りゆう]で、 その 授業[じゅぎょう]は キャンセル されてしまいました。
Because there were too few students registered for it, that class ended up being cancelled.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain という理由で "because" (lit. for the reason that~) is used to present the reason for a state, event, or action stated in the main clause. The phrase is usually used in written language.
家[いえ]に 帰[かえ]って 初[はじ]めて カバンの 中[なか]の 財布[さいふ]が なくなっている ことに 気[き]が ついた。
It was when I returned home that I first realized that my wallet had disappeared from my bag.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S ことに気がつく means: notice (that~); realize that ~ Notice that the presence of こと in a sentence using this grammar may not always be the nominalizer meaning "that." It could be a noun meaning "thing" following the noun-typed usage of this grammar.
万有[ばんゆう] 引力[いんりょく]の 法則[ほうそく] (the law of universal gravitation)は ニュートンに よって 発見[はっけん] されました。
The law of universal gravitation was discovered by Newton.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
~N によって によって indicates the cause, the means, or the agent in passive sentences. In this sentence it indicates AGENT. "because; because of; due to; by V-ing; by means of; via; through; by"
ダイエットの ために 運動[うんどう]を 始[はじ]めたら、 おなかが 空[あ]いて たくさん 食[た]べてしまい、 逆[ぎゃく]に 太[ふと]ってしまった。

逆 に V。 "in the opposite direction; the other way; the wrong way; contrary to one's expectations; contrary to one's intention; conversely" 逆 is used to indicate that X's way of doing something is the opposite of Y's way of doing it, or that the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way Y is or the way Y happens. In different contexts, ぎゃくindicates that X's way of doing something, the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way which is common, expected or intended.
日本[にほん]語[ご]で 数字[すうじ]を １００[ひゃく]から 逆[ぎゃく]に 数[かぞ]えてみて下[くだ]さい。
Try counting backwards (lit. numbers in the opposite direction) from 100 in Japanese, please.

逆 に V。 "in the opposite direction; the other way; the wrong way; contrary to one's expectations; contrary to one's intention; conversely" 逆 is used to indicate that X's way of doing something is the opposite of Y's way of doing it, or that the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way Y is or the way Y happens. In different contexts, ぎゃくindicates that X's way of doing something, the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way which is common, expected or intended.
もう かなり 歩[ある]いた はずなのに、 まだ 目的[もくてき] 地[ち]に 着[つ]かない。 道[みち]に 迷[まよ]ったのだろうか。
We've already walked quite far, but we still haven't reached our destination. I wonder if we're lost.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
かなり "considerably; rather; quite; fairly; pretty; quite a lot; Indicates that the degree of something is not extremely high, but is higher than average.
今日[きょう]は、 雪[ゆき]で 授業[じゅぎょう]を 休[やす]んだ 人[ひと]が 何[なん]人[にん]か いた そうです。
I heard that there were a few people who didn't come to class today because of the snow.

説明 [explanation]: 何(or いく) followed by a counter and か becomes a quantifier meaning "some." 何人か = some people 何枚か = some sheets of paper 何冊か = some books いく＋counter + か is the qualifier "some" Except for the words いくつ and いく人, いく is not commonly used in modern japanese. 何 cannot be used with つ. --- 英訳 [English translation]: some --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {何/いく} + Counter + か
昨日[きのう]は 大雪[おおゆき]で、 授業[じゅぎょう]に 来[き]た 学生[がくせい]は たったの 四[よ]人[にん]だった。
Because of the heavy snow yesterday, only four students showed up for class.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
たった（の）Number (+counter) "only" This is used to emphasize the small amount or number of something.
日本[にほん]の 電車[でんしゃ]や バスに ある シルバー シートと いうは、 お年寄[としよ]りや 体[からだ]の 弱[よわ]い 人[ひと]向[む]けの 席[せき]の ことです。
The Silver Seat found in Japanese trains and buses is a seat for elderly and for weak-bodied people.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N 向けの N2. Means: for; made for; for the use of; directed to The suffix 向け adds the meaning "made for; for the use of; directed toward." 向け is often affixed to nouns which refer to people, countries and organizations.
この 辞書[じしょ]の サイトは 結構[けっこう] 便利[べんり]なので、 よく 使[つか]う。

Grammar,扉,Intermediate
結構 (A/ANa +だ) Means: fairly; pretty; rather; quite The adverb 結構 indicates that the speaker feels that the degree/level/amount/etc. of something is not high, but is higher than average
試験[しけん]の 点[てん]が 良[よ]ければいい 成績[せいせき]が 取[と]れると いう わけでは ない。 宿題[しゅくだい]や プロジェクトも 大切[たいせつ]だ。
You can't count on getting good grades just because you score well on tests. Homework and projects are important, too.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{N/ANo} {という／だった／じゃない／じゃなかった} わけではない Means: It's not that~; It doesn't mean that used to deny a statement.
先生[せんせい]は、 学生[がくせい]が 分[わ]かる ように 易[やさ]しい 単語[たんご]を 使[つか]って 説明[せつめい] した。
The teacher explained using easy vocabulary words so that the students could understand.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) This construction is used to state either a purpose or the way in which something is to be done. In XようにY, X represents a state or event which is beyond the control of the subject of Y. The verb form before ように is often a potential form or a negative form. (2) In the similar construction XためにY, X represents an action which can be controlled by the subject of Y, while XようにY implies that a certain consequence (X) will arise as the result of an action (Y). --- 英訳 [English translation]: so that ~; in such a way that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.nonpastように
それぞれの 国[くに]には、 それぞれの 文化[ぶんか]や 習慣[しゅうかん]が ある。

それぞれ のN Means: each; one's own; in one's own way それぞれ is used to focus on each individual or thing in a group of people or things, and means "each (one of them)."

説明 [explanation]: V-teくる and V-teいく indicate the temporal or spatial direction of an action from the speaker's viewpoint. V-teくる is used when an action appears to be directed toward the speaker, and V-teいく is used when it appears to be directed away from the speaker. V-teくる often indicates that an action or process began in the past and is continuing in the present, or that something has begun to take place. V-teいく, on the other hand, often expresses an action or state that will continue from the present into the future. In other uses, 来る and 行くfollowing V-te maintain their original meanings, i.e., "to come" and "to go." --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-teくる = have V-ed; begin to; become; grow V−teいく = go on V-ing; continue; become; grow --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te来る/行く

漢字[かんじ]を 覚[おぼ]えば 覚[おぼ]えほど、 単語[たんご]の 数[かず]が ますます 増[ふ]えて、 ますます 日本[にほん]語[ご]が 分[わ]かる ようになります。

ますます(~)V "more and more; -er and -er; increasingly; even more; even -er; still more; still -er" ますます occurs with verbs, the adverbial forms of adjectives and adverbs. 第一 のN "first; first of all; to begin with; the first; the primary"

一応 "for the time being; for now; tentatively; although not perfectly; sort of; just in case" In this sentence the use means "for the time being" 一応 is used when an action/state is tentative or not quite complete, perfect or satisfactory. It is also used when an action is taken as a precaution.

This phrase is often used in the passive form Xが問題にされる. Xが問題になる is also common. The meaning is the same as that of the passive version.

説明 [explanation]: をもとにして is a compound particle meaning "based on."して here is optional. The noun-modification form is をもとにした. --- 英訳 [English translation]: based on --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nをもとに(して) N1をもとにしたN2

{V/A} -plain はず [seen here] ANa {な/じゃない/だった/じゃなかった) N {の/じゃない/だった/じゃなかった} "Should; I expect that ~; I believe that~" The dependent noun はず indicates that the speaker/writer or someone he/she empathizes with believes or expects that what is stated before はず is true based on his/her knowledge or memory at the moment of speech or at the time of the event stated in the main clause. The negative form can be either 〜ないはずだ or 〜はずがない.However, the sense of negation is stronger in はずがない. When Sはずだ modifies a noun, の must be used between はず and the noun.

説明 [explanation]: (1) When そういう, こういう and ああいう refer to something/someone the speaker sees or perceives, they are used for something/someone close to the hearer, close to the speaker, and away from both the speaker and the hearer respectively. (2) These phrases are also used to refer to something/someone the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned. Specifically, そういう is used when the speaker has just mentioned something/someone. こういう is used when the speaker has just stated something factual about something/someone. And ああいう is used when the information the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned is known to both. --- 英訳 [English translation]: that/this kind of; such --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {そう/こう/ああ}いうN

N 向けの N2. Means: for; made for; for the use of; directed to The suffix 向け adds the meaning "made for; for the use of; directed toward." 向け is often affixed to nouns which refer to people, countries and organizations.

N+的 the suffix is attached to nouns to make them な-adjectives. When these adj modify nouns, the な is sometimes omitted.

~(ような）気がする Meaning; I feel that~: I have a feeling that ~; have the impression that ~; it seems to me that~ It indicates that the speaker is not certain about something, but has the feeling that it's true. ような can be dropped without changing the meaning.

説明 [explanation]: (1) Sentence など(は) is an abbreviated form of S などということは, which means "things like S." (2) Noun など(は) is a shortened form of Noun などという{もの/人/etc.}は, which means "things/people/etc. like N." なんで is a colloquial version of など(は). V-masu 出す Means: V out; begin to V; start to V; begin V-ing; start V-ing V出す differs from V始める in that V出す is used for abrupt and non-volitional actions, while V始める is used for both volitional and non-volitional actions but NOT for actions which begin abruptly. 説明 [explanation]: Noun さえ with a verb conditional form is used when the condition presented in the clause is the only condition to make the statement in the main clause true. さえ replaces が and を in this structure; however, when other particles occur with さえ here, they do not drop. --- 英訳 [English translation]: If~ only ~; If~ just ~; as long as; --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N( = clause X) さえ V-cond (= clause Y)

（そんな／あんな／こんな）N そんな／あんな： Means: that kind of ~; ~like that あんな： Means: this kind of ~; ~ like this these words are synonymous with そういう、ああいう、こういう respectively and are a bit more colloquial than them.

説明 [explanation]: って is a colloquial topic marker. It often appears in questions. In written language, は can be used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Speaking of ~, As for ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N って

Speaking of "famous places of Japan," you can't forget about onsens.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ~と言えば, which literally means "if you say that--," is used to present, as the topic, something or someone that has just been mentioned by the hearer or speaker. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Speaking of ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ X と言えば (X is usually a noun phrase)
先生[せんせい]の 言[い]った こと、 ノートに 書[か]いとかないと、 忘[わす]れちゃうよ。
If you don't write down what the professor says, you end up forgetting it, you know.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
In casual conversation contracted forms are commonly used.
今日[きょう]、 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]るんでは ないでしょうか。
Today I think it might rain.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This ending indicates the speaker's conjecture and is used to express an opinion in an indecisive fashion. Although the negative form ではない is used, there is no negative meaning. のではない{だろう/でしょう}か are used only in written language, and のではないだろうか is the more formal form. ん{ではないでしょうか/じゃないかな} are used only in spoken language. んじゃないかな is more casual. --- 英訳 [English translation]: I think that ~; Isn't it that~? --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Sのではないでしょうか。
家[いえ]を 出[で]ようと したら、 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]ってきた。
When I was about to leave the house, it started to rain.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-volとした, the past form of V-volとする(to try to do ~), is used in situations when someone had made an attempt to do something but failed, where someone was going to do something but didn't, or where something happened when someone was going to do something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-volとした{が／けれど} = tried to ~, but; was going to ~, but V-volとしたら = when ~ was going to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-volとした{が／けれど}: 行こうとした{が／けれど／ら}; 食べようとした{が／けれど／ら}
今日[きょう]は 朝[あさ]から ずっと 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]った。
It's been raining ever since this morning.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ずっと "all the time; all along; all the way; all through ~; throughout~; ever (since); never (since)" ずっと means that a state or action is ongoing, from one point in time to another point in time (often the moment of speech)
昨夜[さくや]から 今朝[けさ]に かけて、 たくさん 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]った。
We had lots of rain from last night through this morning.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 から N2 にかけて "from N1 to N2" indicates a span of time or space and is used primarily in written language.
雨[あめ]が 強[つよ]く 降[ふ]ってきたにも かかわらず、 サッカーの 試合[しあい]は 続[つづ]けられた。
Despite the fact that it began to rain hard, the soccer match continued.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

X にもかかわらず Y where X is {V/A}-plain ANa {な／じゃない／だった／じゃなかった} N {の／じゃない／だった／じゃなかった} "in spite of (the fact that ~); despite (the fact that ~); although; though; nevertheless" This construction is used to mean "Y in spite of X." It is used when Y is the case even though Y is not usually expected from X.
子供[こども]達[たち]が 幸[しあわ]せな 人生[じんせい]が 送[おく]れる ようにと 願[ねが]っています。
I hope that the children can be sent a happy life.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain.nonpast ように（と）願う Means: hope that ~ And is used to express the speaker's hope or desire that what is stated in the sentence will become a reality.
アラビア語[ご]は、 日本[にほん]語[ご]や ロシア語[ご]と 並[なら]んで 難[むずか]しい 言葉[ことば]だと 言[い]われている。
Arabic, along with languages like Japanese and Russian, is said to be a difficult language to learn.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N と並んで "as well as; just like" Is used when introducing one or more examples to be compared to the subject of the sentence. It is used primarily in written language.
この 大学[だいがく]の ビジネス学[がく] 部[ぶ]は、 医学[いがく] 部[ぶ]と 並[なら]んでは いるのが 難[むずか]しいらしい。
I hear that the business school at this university, just like the medical school, is hard to get into.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N と並んで "as well as; just like" Is used when introducing one or more examples to be compared to the subject of the sentence. It is used primarily in written language.
「すごい」や 「かわいい」などは、 若[わか]い 人[ひと]達[たち]が よく 使[つか]う 表現[ひょうげん]だ。 (=～などと いう 言葉[ことば]は)
Words like "awesome" or "cute" are expressions often used by young people.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) Sentence など(は) is an abbreviated form of S などということは, which means "things like S." (2) Noun など(は) is a shortened form of Noun などという{もの/人/etc.}は, which means "things/people/etc. like N." なんで is a colloquial version of など(は). (3) When S is a quotation, Sなどと is an abbreviated form of S などということを. --- 英訳 [English translation]: things/people/etc. like ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N{など(は)/なんて}: 子供{など(は)/なんて}
最近[さいきん]、 若[わか]い 人[ひと]の 間[あいだ]で 言葉[ことば]の 使[つか]い方[かた]に 変化[へんか]が 見[み]られる。
You can see changes recently in the way young people are using language.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 見られる is the passive form of 見る and means "be observed." 見られる can also be interpreted as the potential form of 見る, in which case it means "can observe/see" --- 英訳 [English translation]: (something) is observed; (one) can observe/see --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nが見られる
私[わたし]は、 最近[さいきん]、 日本[にほん]の 若者[わかもの] 言語[げんご]を 中心[ちゅうしん]と した 言語[げんご]の 研究[けんきゅう]を しています。
Lately, I am making the language of young Japanese people the focus of my language research.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1を中心(と/に)した N2 (= N1中心のN2) "(centering) around; focusing on; mainly; with N as the center/focus/leader/etc." N1を中心(と/に)する literally means "to make N the center." This phrase takes 2 forms. The form used here is used to modify nouns. The phrase indicates that something takes place around N or with N as the center/focus, or that someone does something focusing on N.
日本[にほん]の 若[わか]い 人[ひと]たちと 友達[ともだち]に なりたかったら、 「です・ます」の 話[はな]し方[かた]の 代[か]わりに、 カジュアルな 話[はな]し方[かた]で 話[はな]した ほうが いいよ。
If you want to make friends with young Japanese, you should use casual speech instead of the desu/masu form.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: の代わりに is used to present something/someone that is replacing or has replaced something/someone. When the context is clear, Noun の can be omitted. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in place of; instead of; to make up for --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nの代わりに
この アパートは 駅[えき]に 近[ちか]くて 便利[べんり]な ことは 便利[べんり]だけれど、 家賃[やちん]は とても 高[たか]いです。
It's true that this apartment is close to the station and is convenient, but the rent is really high.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ANa {な/だった} ことは ANa {だ/だった} が "It is certainly true that ~, but; indeed ~, but; do V ~, but; ~ is/are/was/etc. ~, but" This structure is used when the speaker/writer admits that the proposition is true but wants to qualify the proposition with an additional remark.
毎月[まいつき] もらう 給料[きゅうりょう]の うち、 2[に]割[わり]は 家賃[やちん]の ために 使[つか]います。
Twenty percent of my monthly salary goes towards paying rent.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N のうち(で) "in; of; among" Xのうち(で）is used to indicate the total entity (X) when presenting a part or portion of X.
経済[けいざい]は 政治[せいじ]と 深[ふか]い 関係[かんけい]が ある。
Economics is profoundly related to politics.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 は N2 {と／に}関係がある。 This sentence is used to show that N1 is related in someway to N2. The particle after N1 may be と or に。 When this pattern is used in relative clauses, の is commonly used after 関係 instead of が。
1980[せんきゅうひゃくはちじゅう]年[ねん] 代[だい]の 後半[こうはん]から 1990[せんきゅうひゃくきゅうじゅう]年[ねん] 代[だい]の 初[はじ]めに かけての 日本[にほん]の 経済[けいざい]は 「バブル 経済[けいざい]」と 呼[よ]ばれている。
Japan's economy from the latter half of the 1980s through the beginning of the 1990s is referred to as a "bubbly economy".
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
1900/1910/1920/etc. + 年代 "1990s/1910s/1920s/etc." the suffix 代 is used with 10 or its multiples and 年 to refer to a certain decade.
アジアに おける 歴史[れきし]に 関[かん]する 問題[もんだい]は、 解決[かいけつ]が 難[むずか]し そうです。
Resolving the disputes in Asia regarding history looks difficult.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 における N2 "in;at;on;during" The compound particle における indicate the place or time of an action, event, or state. The pre-verbal form is において. Both are used only in formal language.
道後[どうご] 温泉[おんせん]は 日本[にほん]の 一番[いちばん] 古[ふる]い 温泉[おんせん]で、 ３０００[さんぜん]年[ねん]の 歴史[れきし]が 有[あ]ると 言[い]われています。
It is said that the Dougo Onsen, with 3000 years of history, is the oldest onsen in Japan.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to introduce something commonly said about something or someone. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~ it is said to be ~, It is said that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ーはSentence-plainと言われている
A) 今日[きょう]、 田中[たなか]さん、 クラス 休[やす]んだ。 B） そう 言[い]えば、 昨日[きのう]、 おなかが 痛[いた]いって 言[い]ってたよ。 病気[びょうき]かも しれないね。
A) Tanaka missed class today, didn't she? B) Come to think of it, yesterday she said that her stomach hurt. She might be sick.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
そう言えば Means: That reminds me; Now i remember; indeed This conjunctive phrase is used when the speaker is reminded of something by the hearer's remark or the speaker's own remark.
頭[あたま]が 痛[いた]かったので 薬[くすり]を 読[よ]んだら、 かえって ひどくなってしまった。
I took some medicine because I had headache, but that just made it worse.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
かえって "on the contrary; rather"
私[わたし]が 重[おも]い 病気[びょうき]だと いう ことは、 両親[りょうしん]を 除[のぞ]いて だれも 知[し]らない。
Aside from my parents, no one knows that I have a serious disease.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N を除いて "except (for); with the exception of ~; but ~" 除く means "to remove; get rid of." を除いて is used as a compound particle meaning "except."
現代[げんだい]は、 コンピューターが なければ、 暮[く]らしにくい 時代[じだい]に なったと 言[い]えるだろう。
One could say that we've entered an era where it's hard to live without computers.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This pattern is used when the speaker is quite certain that his/her statement is correct but wants to soften the statement so as not to appear too assertive. This is a formal expression. --- 英訳 [English translation]: It probably can be said that ~; it is probably all right to say that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S-plain と言えるだろう
子供[こども]の 時[とき]から 長[なが]い 間[あいだ] 練習[れんしゅう] し続[つづ]けて、 とうとう オリンピックに 参加[さんか] する ことが できた。
I've been practicing ever since I was a child, and now at last I'm getting to compete in the Olympics.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

とうとう V "finally; at (long) last; eventually; in the end; after all" とうとう indicates that an expected situation has occurred after an extended period of time. The adverb ついに is similar to とうとう and can be used in the place of とうとう. ついに is more formal.
日本[にほん]での インターンシップの 経験[けいけん]は、 私[わたし]の 人生[じんせい]を 大[おお]きく 左右[さゆう] するだろう。
My internship experience in Japan will probably have a big impact on my life.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 を N2 左右する "influence; govern" 左右する is most commonly used in written language.
洋風[ようふう]の ホテルも 和風[わふう]の 温泉[おんせん] 旅館[りょかん]も、 どちらも 好[す]きです。
I like Western-style hotels as well as Japanese-style inns with hot springs.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 風の N2 "~style; ~type; look like" 風 is a suffix and is added to nouns to make no-adjectives. X風 means "X style/type" or "looks like X"
お土産[みやげ]に Ｔ シャツを 何[なん]枚[まい]か 買[か]った。
I bought some shirts as souvenirs.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 何(or いく) followed by a counter and か becomes a quantifier meaning "some." 何人か = some people 何枚か = some sheets of paper 何冊か = some books いく＋counter + か is the qualifier "some" Except for the words いくつ and いく人, いく is not commonly used in modern japanese. 何 cannot be used with つ. --- 英訳 [English translation]: some --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {何/いく} + Counter + か
明日[あした]に なっても 犬[いぬ]が 見付[みつ]からない 場合[ばあい]は、 ペット レスキュー センターに 探[さが]しに 行[い]きましょう。
In case we don't find the dog tomorrow, let's go look for it at the pet rescue center.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 場合 is a noun meaning "case, occasion, situation," but with a modifier it forms an adverbial phrase/clause meaning "when; if; in case." 時 can be used in place of 場合 as seen in this example: 分からない {時／場合} は、言って下さい。 However, 場合 cannot replace 時 when 時 refers to a specific time and does not mean "case; occasion; situation," as shown in the example below: 私が行った {時／ｘ場合}には、ミーティングが始まっていた。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: if; when; in case --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ DemA + 場合: {この/その/あの} 場合
スポーツを 通[とお]して、 子供[こども]たちは とても 仲良[なかよ]く なりました。
Through sports, the children became good friends.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N を通して "through; via" を通して indicates a medium (X) through which someone does something or something happens. X can be things, people, activities or actions.
私[わたし]は 健康[けんこう]の ため、 エレベーターに 乗[の]らないで 階段[かいだん]を 使[つか]う ことに しています。
To maintain my health, I make a habit of taking the stairs instead of the elevator.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by a noun or the non-past form of a verb, it indicates either purpose or reason/cause. In different contexts, Noun のため(に) also indicates benefit, as seen in the example sentence in this flashcard. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in order to; to; for the purpose of; for; for the sake of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nのため(に) N1のためのN2 Verb plainため(に) Verb plainためのN
電車[でんしゃ]に 乗[の]ろうと したら、 目[め]の 前[まえ]で ドアが 閉[し]まってしまった。
Just as I was about to get on the train, the doors closed before my eyes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-volとした, the past form of V-volとする(to try to do ~), is used in situations when someone had made an attempt to do something but failed, where someone was going to do something but didn't, or where something happened when someone was going to do something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-volとした{が／けれど} = tried to ~, but; was going to ~, but V-volとしたら = when ~ was going to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-volとした{が／けれど}: 行こうとした{が／けれど／ら}; 食べようとした{が／けれど／ら}
コンビニには、 生活[せいかつ] 用品[ようひん]でも 食[た]べ物[もの]でも 雑誌[ざっし]や 新聞[しんぶん]でも、 なんでも 置[お]いてある。
They've got everything at convenience stores, from everyday essentials to food to magazines and newspapers.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 でも N2 でも "including X and Y; whether (it is) X or Y" This is used to provide examples for the statement in the sentence. This structure implies that there are also things other than the examples which make the statement true. Note that XもYも (both X and Y) does not carry such an implication..
「電気[でんき]の 町[まち]」 秋葉原[あきはばら]は、 最近[さいきん] 「お宅[たく]の 町[まち]」だとも 言[い]われている。
Akihabara is said to be "Electronics Town", but now it is said that it's "Otaku Town"
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to introduce something commonly said about something or someone. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~ it is said to be ~, It is said that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ーはSentence-plainと言われている
1[いち]年[ねん]に 700万[ななれいれいまん]人[にん] 以上[いじょう]の 人[ひと]が 訪[おとず]れると いう。
It is said over 7 million visit each year.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain という "It is said that ~; They say that ~" This structure indicate that the preceding information is not first hand. This is a polite form.
予定[よてい]が 思[おも]う ように 進[すす]まないので、 とても 困[こま]っています。
The schedule is not going as planned and I'm having a lot of trouble.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

思うように〜ない [->typically, ~ is V-potential] "not ~ as one wishes" This phrase means that something is not in accord with the speaker's/writer's (or the subject's) wish or desire. The verb potential form is usually used in this structure.)
子供[こども]の 時[とき]、 アニメが 大好[だいす]きだったんだ。 それで、 日本[にほん]語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] しようと 思[おも]ったんだ。
When I was a child I loved anime. Because of that I thought I would study Japanese.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: It is a sentence-initial conjunction. It precedes a fact, conclusion, decision, etc. S1 is the cause/reason for the information stated in S2. それで cannot be used when S2 is the speaker's judgement, request or command. In this situation, だから should be used. Note that だから can be used in situations where それで is used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: because of that; so; that's why; for that reason --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S１。それで、S２。
トムさんは 昨日[きのう] よく 勉強[べんきょう] していたから、 今日[きょう]の 日本[にほん]語[ご]の 試験[しけん]、 簡単[かんたん]だったでしょ。
Tom, you studied hard last night, so I guess your Japanese test today was easy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: でしょう and だろう with rising intonation are used to elicit the hearer's confirmation. でしょう is the polite version of だろう. In casual conversation, male speakers use だろう and female speakers use でしょう. In more casual situations, the final う tends to drop. Note: でしょう and だろう with falling intonation indicate conjecture. --- 英訳 [English translation]: tag question(e.g. isn't it?; wasn't it?; aren't they?; is he?; are they?) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~だろう, ~でしょう
子供[こども]の うちに 外国[がいこく] 語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] すると 発音[はつおん]が よくなる そうだ。
If you study foreign languages while you're still a child you can develop good pronunciation.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (ない)うちに is used when someone does something before a situation or state changes. 間に is used in similar situations, but it cannot be used with the negative forms of verbs. Another difference between the two phrases is that うちに always implies that it is not possible, easy or a good idea to do something after the time specified by the うちに clause. However, this is not always the case with 間に. Thus far, if it is not a problem for the speaker to go to Japan after finishing his Japanese class, 間に should be used, as shown below: 日本語の勉強をしている間に日本に行ってみたい。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: while ~ still ～ないうちに＝ before (something happens) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ～うちに
できれば 医者[いしゃ]に なりたいが、 授業[じゅぎょう]料[りょう]が 高[たか]いので 難[むずか]しいかも しれない。
If possible, I would like to become a doctor, but the tuition cost is expensive so it'll probably be difficult to do.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The phrase literally means "if possible." It is also used when the speaker asks a favor of someone in a less direct way. できれば is slightly more formal than できたら. --- 英訳 [English translation]: if possible; if you don't mind; if it's all right --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ できれば／できたら
私[わたし]が 今[こん]学期[がっき] 取[と]っている 授業[じゅぎょう]の うちで、 宿題[しゅくだい]が ないのは タンスの クラスだけだ。
Out of the classes I'm taking this semester, the only one with no homework is dance.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N のうち(で) "in; of; among" Xのうち(で）is used to indicate the total entity (X) when presenting a part or portion of X.
子供[こども]同士[どうし]の けんかが 原因[げんいん]で、 親[おや]同士[どうし]の 関係[かんけい]も 悪[わる]くなってしまった。
A fight between the children also caused the relationship between the two sets of parents to sour.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N同士 {が／で／を} Indicates that Ns do something together, that Ns do something to/for/against each other, or that someone puts Ns together in some way.
日本[にほん]語[ご]では、 目上[めうえ]の 人[ひと]に 対[たい]して 「あなた」と 呼[よ]ぶのは とても 失礼[しつれい]な ことだ。
In Japanese, it's very rude to address your superiors as "anata".
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N に対して "toward; for; in; with regard to" This grammar marks something to/toward/about which one does something, or mark someone to/toward whom one does something or owes something. In different contexts, it can mark something one has interest in. Do not confuse with the use where に対して indicates two contrasting actions, states, situations, etc.
日本[にほん]と 私[わたし]の 国[くに]は、 朝[あさ]と 夜[よる]が 逆[ぎゃく]だ。 いま、 こちらは 午後[ごご] ９[く]時[じ]だが、 日本[にほん]は 午前[ごぜん] １０[じゅう]時[じ]だ。
The mornings and evenings in my country are opposite that of Japan. Here it is 9PM, but in Japan it is 10AM.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

X は 逆 だ。 "be opposite; the other way" 逆 is used to indicate that X's way of doing something is the opposite of Y's way of doing it, or that the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way Y is or the way Y happens. In different contexts, ぎゃくindicates that X's way of doing something, the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way which is common, expected or intended.
アパートは 駅[えき]に 近[ちか]ければ 近[ちか]いほど 家賃[やちん]が 高[たか]くなり、 逆[ぎゃく]に、 駅[えき]から 遠[とおざ]ければ 遠[とお]いほど 安[やす]くなる。
The closer an apartment is to the train station to more expensive rent becomes. Inversely, the farther an apartment is from the train stations, the cheaper it becomes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-cond {V/A}-plain ほど "the (more) ~, the (more) ~" This structure is used when the more something happens or is in some state, the more another thing happens or is in some state. (When V is a suru verb, the second VN is usually omitted)
困[こま]っている 人[ひと]が いたら 迷[まよ]わず 助[たす]けて上[あ]げる。
If there are people in trouble, I give help without hesitating.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ずに is synonymous with ないで when ないで means "without doing something" or "instead of doing something." に is sometimes omitted. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Without V-ing; instead of V-ing --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-naiずに: 行かずに; 食べずに (Exception: する->せずに
九州[きゅうしゅう]か 四国[しこく]へ 行[い]く。 本[ほん]か 雑誌[ざっし]が ある。 友達[ともだち]か 家族[かぞく]と 旅行[りょこう]に 行[い]く。
I will go either to kyushu or shikoku. There are either books or magazines. I will go travel with either my friends or family.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The phrase AかBか is used to present alternatives. When Bか is followed by a case particle (e.g., が, を, へ, に, で, と), the second か is usually dropped. --- 英訳 [English translation]: either A or B; whether A or B --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. 〜か〜か b. N1かN2+Particle
台風[たいふう]が 近[ちか]いづいている ため、 九州[きゅうしゅう]を 中心[ちゅうしん]に 大雨[おおあめ]が 降[ふ]っている。
Due to the approaching typhoon, heavy rain is falling, centered in Kyushu.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N を 中心 {と/に} (して） "(centering) around; focusing on; mainly; with N as the center/focus/leader/etc." Nを中心(と/に)する literally means "to make N the center." This phrase takes 2 forms. The form used here is used to modify verbs. The phrase indicates that something takes place around N or with N as the center/focus, or that someone does something focusing on N.
今年[ことし]は あまり 雪[ゆき]が 降[ふ]らない。 その ために スキーが 出来[でき]ない。
There hasn't been much snow this year. Because of that, we can't go skiing.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by an i-adjective or a na-adjective or the past form of a verb, it indicates reason or cause. When it is preceded by the non-past form of a verb or a noun, it means either reason/cause or purpose. The meaning is determined from the context. Whenため(に) means reason/cause, it can be replaced by 〜から or 〜ので, which are less formal than 〜ために. --- 英訳 [English translation]: because; due to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {この/その/あの}ため(に)
ハワイは １[いち]年[ねん] 中気[ちゅうき]温[おん]が 高[たか]いけれど、 高[たか]い 山[やま]では 雪[ゆき]が 降[ふ]る 事[こと]も 有[あ]る そうだ。
Hawaii is warm all year around, but I hear that there are times when it snows in the high mountains.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain-nonpast ことがある is used when something occurs (or someone does something) occasionally. も implies that something else may also occur. Note: This phrase should not be confused with V-plain-PAST ことがある (e.g. 日本に行ったことがある。) which states previous experience. --- 英訳 [English translation]: There are times when ~, sometimes --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain-nonpast こと{が / も}ある
量[りょう]は 多[おお]かったけれど、 お腹[なか]が すいていたから、 ほとんど 食[た]べてしまった。
There was a lot of food, but I was hungry, so I ate almost all of it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ほとんど V Means "almost all; most of (it, the time, etc.)" It is only used with the amount of something is the issue.
おいしい 料理[りょうり]だったが、 お腹[なか]が 痛[いた]くて ほとんど 食[た]べられなかった。
The food was good, but I had a stomachache,so I could barely eat anything.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ほとんど〜ない。 means: hardly (ever); rarely; almost no(thing)
今[いま]、 食[た]べたばかりですから, お腹[なか]が いっぱいで、 何[なに]も 食[た]べられません。
I just ate, and I'm so full that I really can't eat another bite.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.past ばかり indicates that someone has just done something or something has just happened. The noun modification form is ばかりの. --- 英訳 [English translation]: have just V-ed --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.past ばかりだ V-plain.past ばかりの N
赤[あか]ちゃんが 泣[な]いてばかり いるので、 母親[ははおや]に なったばかりの 洋子[ようこ]さんは とても 困[こま]っている。
The baby cries all the time, so Yoko, who has just become a mother, is at it wits' end.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V−te ばかりいる。 Means: Nothing But; always; all the time ばかり is used to express the idea that someone does one thing all the time and does nothing else, or that someone chooses just one thing among others when doing something. Ex: 田中さんはマンガばかり読んでいる。 can mean: (= All tanaka does is read comics); (= Tanaka reads only comics); (=When Masao reads, he reads nothing but comics) NOTE: ばっかり is more colloquial than ばかり
大学[だいがく]に 近[ちか]くて 便利[べんり]だって 言[い]っても、 家賃[やちん]が 高[たか]すぎるから、 この 部屋[へや]は 借[か]りられない。
Even if its location is close to the university, the rent for this room is too high for me to rent it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-plain {と/って} 言っても "although ~ say/said that ~; even though ~ say/said that ~" Its used to clarify what has just been said in order to avoid misunderstanding. って is used in place of と in casual conversation or writing.
この アパートは 家賃[やちん]が 安[やす]いから、 静[しず]かでも 静[しず]か {じゃ/で} なくても、 借[か]りようと 思[おも]っています。
The rent for this apartment is cheap, so whether it's quiet or not I'm thinking about renting it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{ANa/ANo/N} でも {ANa/ANo/N} {じゃ／で} なくても "whether X or not"
どんな アパートを 借[か]りるかは、 家賃[やちん] 次第[しだい]だ。
What type of apartment I rent depends on the rent.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N次第だ "depend on N" When 次第 is affixed to nouns, it means "depend on."
郵便[ゆうびん] 局[きょく]に 行[い]って来[こ]なくちゃん ないから、 ちょっと ここで 待[ま]ってて。
I've gotta run to the post office, so wait here for a sec.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: These patterns express the idea of obligation. Although the two patterns are interchangeable, there is a subtle difference between ならない and いけない. That is, ならない is commonly used when the speaker states his/her sense of obligation while いけない is commonly used when the sense of obligation is directed towards the hearer (i.e. when the speaker wants to impose a certain obligation on the hearer). The following contracted forms are used in casual conversation: なきゃならない -> なきゃなんない なくちゃならない -> なくちゃんなんない --- 英訳 [English translation]: have to; must; should --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜なければ{いけない/ならない} 〜なくては{いけない/ならない}
よく 切[き]れない 包丁[ほうちょう]は かえって 危[あぶ]ないよ。
Dull knives are actually all the more dangerous, you know.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
かえって "on the contrary; rather"
危[あぶ]ないですから、 この フィンスの 中[なか]に 決[けっ]して 入[はい]っては いけませんよ。
It's dangerous, so you absolutely must not enter into this fenced area.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
決して{ANa/ANo/N} {では/じゃ} { ない／なかった／ありません／ありませんでした}
A: スミスさんは、 将来[しょうらい] 日本[にほん]の 会社[かいしゃ]で 働[はたら]くのが 夢[ゆめ]なんだって。 B: へー、 スミスさんが そんな 夢[ゆめ]を 持[も]っているなんて、 絶対[ぜったい] 知[し]らなかった。
A: They say Ms. Smith's dream is to work at a Japanese company in the future. B: Really? I had no idea she had a dream like that.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
（そんな／あんな／こんな）N そんな／あんな： Means: that kind of ~; ~like that あんな： Means: this kind of ~; ~ like this these words are synonymous with そういう、ああいう、こういう respectively and are a bit more colloquial than them.
将来[しょうらい]は、 ヨーロッパ、 あるいは、 アジアで 仕事[しごと]が できたらいいと 思[おも]っている。
I think it'd be nice if I can work in Europe or Asia in the future.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1(、N2、〜）あるいは Nn "or; either ~ or ~" あるいは is used to connect alternatives. It is usually used in formal speech or written language.
将来[しょうらい]は、 自分[じぶん]の 能力[のうりょく]を 生[い]かす ことが 出来[でき]る 会社[かいしゃ]で 働[はたら]きたい。
In the future, I want to work at a company that puts my skills to good use.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
生かす "make the most of; make the best use of; use effectively; maintain" 生かす means literally "to keep alive," but it is also used to mean "to make the most of one's ability, etc"
将来[しょうらい]、 日本[にほん]の 会社[かいしゃ]で 働[はたら]きたいと 思[おも]っている。 その ためには もっと 日本[にほん]語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]にならなくては いけない。
In the future, I want to work at a Japanese company. For that purpose, I need to become more skilled at Japanese.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by a noun or the non-past form of a verb, it indicates either purpose or reason/cause. In different contexts, Noun のため(に) also indicates benefit. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in order to; to; for the purpose of; for; for the sake of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nのため(に) N1のためのN2 Verb plainため(に) Verb plainためのN
将来[しょうらい]、 小[しょう]学校[がっこう]の 先生[せんせい]に なりたいと 思[おも]っています。 そこで、 ボランティアで 子供[こども]達[たち]を 教[おし]えてみる ことに しました。
I'm thinking that I want to become an elementary school teacher in the future, so I've decided to try teaching children on a volunteer basis.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1, そこで, S2. "Because of that; therefore; so" そこで is used to indicate and action (to be) taken because of the situation presented in S1. それで may replace そこで そこで may only replace それで when S2 is a controllable action. ex. 寒かった。それで、見に来た人が少なかった。 only それで can be used here.
せっかく 4[よん]年間[ねんかん]も 日本[にほん]語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] したのに、 大学[だいがく]を 卒業[そつぎょう] してから あまり 使[つか]わなかったら、 だんだん 忘[わす]れてしまった。
I put in four whole years studying Japanese, but I haven't used it much since I graduated from the university, so now bit by bit I'm forgetting it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
だんだん "gradually; little by little; bit by bit" だんだん is used to indicate that a state changes gradually. Thus, it often occurs with ~ていく; 〜てくる；〜くなる；〜になる；〜ようになる
この 大学[だいがく]では、 日本[にほん]語[ご]、 あるいは、 英語[えいご]で 卒業[そつぎょう] 論文[ろんぶん]を 書[か]く ことに なっている。
At this university, senior theses are expected to be written in either Japanese or English.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1(、N2、〜）あるいは Nn "or; either ~ or ~" あるいは is used to connect alternatives. It is usually used in formal speech or written language.
とうとう 博士[はかせ] 論文[ろんぶん]が 完成[かんせい] した。 5[ご]年[ねん]も かかってしまった。
My doctoral dissertation is finally complete. It took me five whole years.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
