Note that this phrase differs from Vことにする, which indicates one's decision to do something and the action can be either a single or habitual one. --- 英訳 [English translation]: make an effort to~; make an effort so that~; try (one's best) to do ~; try one's best so that~. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-pastようにする: {食べる/食べない}ようにする
自分[じぶん]で、 部屋[へや]は、 毎日[まいにち]ちゃんと 掃除[そうじ] して、 きちんと 片付[かたづ]けておきなさいよ。
You need to clean your room properly and put things in their proper places every day.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ちゃんと；きちんと "neatly; tidily; properly; adequately; in good order; regularly; without fail" ちゃんと and きちんと both indicate that someone does something neatly, properly, regularly, or without fail (i.e. in the way it is supposed to be done). ちゃんと is more colloquial than きちんと。
私[わたし]の 弟[おとうと]は １[いっ]歳[さい]の 時[とき]、 歩[ある]き始[はじ]めました。 そして、 １[いっ]歳[さい] 半[はん]に 成[な]った 時[とき]、 話[はな]し始[はじ]めました。
My little brother started walking when he was one year old, and then he started talking when he was one and a half.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
説明 [explanation]: 始める in this use is an auxiliary verb meaning "begin to V." --- 英訳 [English translation]: begin to, begin-V-ing --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Verb-masu 始める
あの 殺人[さつじん] 事件[じけん]から もう 5[ご]年[ねん]も たっているのに、 未[いま]だに 犯人[はんにん]は 捕[つか]まっていない。
It's been five years since that murder (case), but the killer still hasn't been caught.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
未だに "still; (not ~) yet" indicates that someone of something is in the same state as he/she/it was some time ago. This form is primarily used in written language. In spoken language まだ is used.
毎日[まいにち] 寝[ね]る 前[まえ]に、 新[あたら]しい 漢字[かんじ]を 五つ[いつつ] 覚[おぼ]える ようにしています。
I'm trying to learn five new kanji before going to bed every night.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.non-pastようにする: indicates one's conscious effort to do something for some purpose. Here one makes an effort at every opportunity to do something to the degree that he or she can, but sometimes fails. Thus ようにする is often used for habitual actions. Note that this phrase differs from Vことにする, which indicates one's decision to do something and the action can be either a single or habitual one. --- 英訳 [English translation]: make an effort to~; make an effort so that~; try (one's best) to do ~; try one's best so that~. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-pastようにする: {食べる/食べない}ようにする
同[おな]じ 漢字[かんじ] また 間違[まちが]えた。
I got the same kanji wrong again.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: In addition to the meaning "again," また expresses the meaning "also" or "additionally." --- 英訳 [English translation]: also; as well; additionally; in addition; moreover --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ また、S。
あの 喫茶[きっさ]店[てん]では コーヒーが たったの 200[にひゃく]円[えん]で 飲[の]める そうだ。
I heard that you can get coffee for just 200 yen at that coffee shop.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
たった（の）Number (+counter) "only" This is used to emphasize the small amount or number of something.
妹[いもうと]は 怖[こわ]くて 夜[よる] 眠[ねむ]れなくなる くせに、 ホラー ムービーばかり 見[み]ている。
Even though she gets scared and can't sleep, my little sister always watches horror films.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

〜くせに Means: Although~; in spite of the fact that~; and yet~ This conjunction is used when something commonly expected from information in the subordinate clause (i.e. the くせに phrase/clause) does not happen or is not the case. In most situations, くせに expresses the speaker's anger, frustration or disagreement. This emotion is not directed toward the speaker, but toward the hearer or 3rd person. When くせに is used, the subject of the main clause and that of the subordinate clause must be the same. If the subjects differ, you must use なのに、.
キッチンから 流[なが]れてくる においから すると、 今日[きょう]の 晩御飯[ばんごはん]は カレー ライスかなあ。
The smell from the kitchen makes me think we're having curry tonight.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Nからすると "judging from~" Introduces the source or basis for the speaker's conjecture or judgment. The information can be of any sort including visual or verbal.
若[わか]い 人[ひと]の 方[ほう]が、 年[とし]を 取[と]った 人[ひと]より、 ファースト フードを よく 食[た]べると いう 傾向[けいこう]が 見[み]られる。
Young people, more so than old people, tend to eat fast food often.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-plain.nonpast (という)傾向が見られる。 Means: Have a tendency to; have an inclination to; There is a tendency to; tend to This construction is used when someone or something has a tendency to do something. It is commonly used in written language and formal speech. という is optional.
日本[にほん]の 学生[がくせい]は 高校[こうこう]までは よく 勉強[べんきょう] するが、 大学[だいがく]に 入[はい]ってからは あまり 勉強[べんきょう] しない 傾向[けいこう]が ある。
There is a tendency for Japanese students to study often through high school, but after getting into a university, not study much.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-plain.nonpast (という)傾向がある。 Means: Have a tendency to; have an inclination to; There is a tendency to; tend to This construction is used when someone or something has a tendency to do something. It is commonly used in written language and formal speech. という is optional.
朝寝[あさね]坊[ぼう]を しない ように、 目覚[めざ]まし 時計[とけい]を セット して置[お]きます。
So that I don't sleep in in the morning, I'll set my alarm clock (in preparation).
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) This construction is used to state either a purpose or the way in which something is to be done. In XようにY, X represents a state or event which is beyond the control of the subject of Y. The verb form before ように is often a potential form or a negative form. (2) In the similar construction XためにY, X represents an action which can be controlled by the subject of Y, while XようにY implies that a certain consequence (X) will arise as the result of an action (Y). --- 英訳 [English translation]: so that ~; in such a way that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.nonpastように
今朝[けさ]、 朝寝[あさね]坊[ぼう] して クラスに 遅[おく]れちゃったから、 明日[あした]は もっと 早[はや]く 起[お]きなくちゃ。
This morning I overslept and ended up being late for class, so I've gotta wake up earlier tomorrow.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: These patterns express the idea of obligation. Although the two patterns are interchangeable, there is a subtle difference between ならない and いけない. That is, ならない is commonly used when the speaker states his/her sense of obligation while いけない is commonly used when the sense of obligation is directed towards the hearer (i.e. when the speaker wants to impose a certain obligation on the hearer). The following contracted forms are used in casual conversation: なきゃならない -> なきゃなんない なくちゃならない -> なくちゃんなんない --- 英訳 [English translation]: have to; must; should --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜なければ{いけない/ならない} 〜なくては{いけない/ならない}
また 朝[あさ] 寝坊[ねぼう] してしまって、 また 授業[じゅぎょう]に 遅[おく]れた。
I overslept again, and again I was late for class.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: In addition to the meaning "again," また expresses the meaning "also" or "additionally." --- 英訳 [English translation]: also; as well; additionally; in addition; moreover --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ また、S。
動物[どうぶつ]園[えん]で パンダの 赤[あか]ちゃんが ３[さん]匹[びき] 生[う]まれた そうだ。 こう いう ニュースは うれしい。
I hear that three baby pandas were born at the zoo. This kind of news makes me happy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) When そういう, こういう and ああいう refer to something/someone the speaker sees or perceives, they are used for something/someone close to the hearer, close to the speaker, and away from both the speaker and the hearer respectively. (2) These phrases are also used to refer to something/someone the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned. Specifically, そういう is used when the speaker has just mentioned something/someone. こういう is used when the speaker has just stated something factual about something/someone. And ああいう is used when the information the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned is known to both. --- 英訳 [English translation]: that/this kind of; such --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {そう/こう/ああ}いうN
暖[あたた]かくなるに つれて、 雪[ゆき]が 溶[と]け、 木[き]が 緑[みどり]に なっていく。
As it becomes warmer, the snow is melting and the trees are turning green.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-non-past.aff につれて "as ~; with ~" Xにつれて indicates that omething takes place as X occurs. X can be either a verb or the stem of a suru-V.
梅雨[つゆ]に 入[はい]ってから、 晴[は]れの 日[ひ]が まったく なくて 湿度[しつど]が 高[たか]く、 気持[きも]ちが 悪[わる]い。
Since the rainy season began, it's been uncomfortable, with no sunny days and lots of humidity.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (time period) に {入り/入って (から)} "since N began; after N began" N に入る literally means "to enter N," but when N is a noun indicating a time period, the phrase means "N begins." The most common form is N に入り or N に入って（から), meaning "since/after N began."
日本[にほん]の 夏[なつ]は とても 暑[あつ]い。 それに 湿度[しつど]も 高[たか]い。
Japan's summers are very sultry. Furthermore, the humidity is also high.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: それに is used to add an item or make an addition statement. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in addition; moreover; furthermore; what's more; on top of that; and --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 {、/と / に} N2, それに N3 b. S1。それに、S2。 c. S1 し、それに、S2。
東京[とうきょう]は 物価[ぶっか]が 高[たか]い ことだけでなく、 土地[とち]も 狭[せま]いので、 暮[く]らしにくいと いうのは 事実[じじつ]だ。
The fact is that Tokyo is a hard place to live in, not only because the prices are high there but also because the land is small (i.e. there are too many people for the land)
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S (という）のは事実だ。 "It is {true/a fact that} ~" Used when the speaker wants to claim that something is true or is a fact, or when he/she admits that something is true or a fact. The presence or absence of という does not change the meaning.
日本[にほん]の 国土[こくど]は 狭[せま] そうに 思[おも]われているが、 数字[すうじ]の 上[うえ]で 見[み]ると、 そうでも ない。
People think of Japan as having a small landmass, but when you look at the numbers, that's not quite the case.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N のうえで "in terms of; from the viewpoint of ~; as far as ~ is concerned; according to ~" Nの上で and N上 are used to indicate that the speaker's statement refers only to N. Commonly used in written language.
「聞[き]くは 一時[いちじ]の 恥[はじ]、 聞[き]かぬは、 一生[いっしょう]の 恥[はじ]」ですよ。だから、 どんどん 質問[しつもん] してください。
You know what they say: "Asking a question makes for momentary embarrassment; not asking makes for a lifetime of shame." Ask as many questions as you like.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-nai ぬ "not" ぬ is a verb ending from classical Japanese and is equivalent to ない in meaning and form. In modern Japanese, it often appears in set phrases.
弟[おとうと]が 大学[だいがく]の 入学[にゅうがく] 試験[しけん]に 合格[ごうかく] できる ように と 毎日[まいにち] 祈[いの]っています。
I pray every day that my little brother will pass his university entrance exams.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V.nonpast.plan. ように（と）祈る Means: pray that ~ Used to express the speaker's hope or desire that what is stated in the sentence will become a reality.
毎年[まいとし] お正月[しょうがつ]に 神社[じんじゃ]に 行[い]って、 今年[ことし]も 大[おお]きな 病気[びょうき]を しない ように 神社[じんじゃ]に 祈[いの]る ことに している。
I make it a habit to go to a shrine every year on New Year's Day and pray to the gods that I'll be able to avoid any major illness during the year.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V.nonpast.plan. ように（と）祈る Means: pray that ~ Used to express the speaker's hope or desire that what is stated in the sentence will become a reality.
地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]の せいで、 グリーンランドの 氷[こおり]が どんどん 溶[と]けて (to melt) いる そうだ。
I heard that due to global warming the ice around Greenland is melting at a fast pace.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

どんどん-V "at a fast pace; one after another; keep V-ing vigorously; with no hesitation; with no delay" どんどん expresses the idea that something proceeds from one stage to the next or continues to happen at a fast pace with no delay, or that someone keeps doing something with no hesitation. In some situations both ますますand どんどん can be used, bearing in mind that ますます does not convey the idea that something happens at a fast pace and cannot describe a controllable future action.
地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]に よって 北極[ほっきょく]の 氷[こおり]が 溶[と]けて (to melt) いるらしい。
I've heard that, as an effect of global warming, the ice in the Arctic is melting.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
~ことによって によって indicates the cause, the means, or the agent in passive sentences. In this sentence it indicates CAUSE. "because; because of; due to; by V-ing; by means of; via; through; by"
生[う]み出[だ]す 見[み]つけ出[だ]す 掘[ほ]り出[だ]す
うみだす - to create みつけだすー to find out ほりだす- to dig up/out
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-masu 出す Means: V out; begin to V; start to V; begin V-ing; start V-ing V出す differs from V始める in that V出す is used for abrupt and non-volitional actions, while V始める is used for both volitional and non-volitional actions but NOT for actions which begin abruptly. V-masu 出す has 2 meanings, here is the (1) Someone makes something available/accessible which hasn't existed or hasn't been available or accessible.
真[ま]っ赤[か]な 夕日[ゆうひ]が 海[うみ]に 沈[しず]んで (to set) いく。
The evening sun, brilliant red, is sinking into the sea.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

真っX where X = adjective or Noun Means: very; pure; totally; right; mid- 真っAdj indicates the degree of something is very high or is at the highest level. 真っNoun indicates the center of a space or time span. The english translation of 真っ varies according to the word that follows it.
熱[あつ]い うちに、 どうぞ 召[め]し上[あ]がって下[くだ]さい。
While it is still hot, please eat. (very polite phrasing)
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (ない)うちに is used when someone does something before a situation or state changes. 間に is used in similar situations, but it cannot be used with the negative forms of verbs. Another difference between the two phrases is that うちに always implies that it is not possible, easy or a good idea to do something after the time specified by the うちに clause. However, this is not always the case with 間に. Thus far, if it is not a problem for the speaker to go to Japan after finishing his Japanese class, 間に should be used, as shown below: 日本語の勉強をしている間に日本に行ってみたい。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: while ~ still ～ないうちに＝ before (something happens) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ～うちに
日本[にほん]語[ご]には 「いらっしゃいます」や 「召[め]し上[あ]がります」など、 いろいろな 敬語[けいご]が ある。
In Japanese, there are various honorific expressions, like irasshaimasu and meshiagarimasu.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: など indicates that the given list is not exhaustive. When more than one item is listed, や is commonly used to connect the item. --- 英訳 [English translation]: N1やN2など = N1, N2 and others. N1やN2などのN3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. N1やN2など、N3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N1やN2など({は / も / が / を / に / の / etc.)} (N1 and N2 can be words or phrases).
この 猫[ねこ]、 拾[ひろ]ってきた ときは 死[し]に そうだったけど、 だんだん 元気[げんき]になったんだ。
When I took in this abandoned cat, it was close to dying, but little by little it's gotten healthier.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
だんだん "gradually; little by little; bit by bit" だんだん is used to indicate that a state changes gradually. Thus, it often occurs with ~ていく; 〜てくる；〜くなる；〜になる；〜ようになる
私[わたし]は 10[じゅう]台[だい]で 結婚[けっこん] して すぐ 子供[こども]を 産[う]み、 40[よんじゅう]台[だい]で 孫[まご]が 産[う]まれ 「 おばあさん」に なりました。
I got married in my teens and had a child right away, and in my forties my first grandchild was born and I became a grandma.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
10/20/30/etc. ＋ 代 "one's teens/twenties/ thirties/etc." The suffix 代 is used with ten or its multiples to describe someone's approximate age.
授業[じゅぎょう]料[りょう]を 幾[いく]ら 払[はら]わなくては 行[い]けないかは、 大学[だいがく]に よって 違[ちが]う。
How much tuition fee you have to pay differs depending on the university.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate that something differs depending on the situation, location, time, etc. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~によって違う = differ depending on ~ / due to ~ による = depend on, due to, according to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {Noun/Question Word ~ か/ ~かどうか}は Noun に {よって違う / よる }
すみません。 学生[がくせい]証[しょう]と いうのは、 何[なん]の ことですか？ 学生[がくせい]証[しょう]と いうのは、 Student IDの ことですよ。
I'm sorry, what does "gakuseishou" mean? It means "student ID".
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The structure ~というのは~だ is used to provide the meaning or definition of a word or phrase. --- 英訳 [English translation]: X means ~; The meaning of X is ~; What X means is ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. ~ というのは {Nのこと / N ということ}だ b. ~ というのは Sことだ. Type 2c c. ~ というのは {Sということ/Sという意味}だ. Type 1
英語[えいご]は 世界[せかい]で 最[もっと]も 使[つか]われている 言葉[ことば]の 一[ひと]つだ。 したがって、 英語[えいご]を 義務[ぎむ] 教育[きょういく]の 中[なか]に 入[い]れている 国[くに]は 多[おお]い。
English is one of the most widely-used languages in the world. As a result, many countries have made the English language a part of their compulsory education.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S1 (reason/cause). したがって、S２ (consequence.) "therefore; accordingly; consequently; as a result; so"
男[おとこ]の子[こ]が 興味[きょうみ]を 持[も]つ オタク 文化[ぶんか]に 対[たい]して、 カワイイ 文化[ぶんか]は 女[おんな]の子[こ]に 人気[にんき]が ある ようだ。
It seems that in contrast to otaku culture, which mostly boys are interested in, kawaii culture is more popular among girls.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Nに対して "whereas; on the other hand; in contrast" に対して is used when contrasting two actions, states, situations, etc.
伝統[でんとう] 芸能[げいのう]を 通[とお]して、 日本[にほん]の 古[ふる]くて 美[うつく]しい 文化[ぶんか]を 学[まな]んだ。
I learned of Japan's old time, beautiful culture through its traditional performing arts.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N を通して "through; via" を通して indicates a medium (X) through which someone does something or something happens. X can be things, people, activities or actions.
アインシュタインは 物理[ぶつり]学[がく]者[しゃ]だった 上[うえ]に、 音楽[おんがく]家[か]と しても 素晴[すば]らしかった そうです。
I've heard that in addition to being a physicist Einstein was also superb musician.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S 上に "in addition to~; besides~; not only~but also~; moreover~; ~ as well" The conjunction 上に introduces additional information emphatically.
日本[にほん]語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] して、 日本[にほん]の 歴史[れきし]に 対[たい]する 興味[きょうみ]が さらに 強[つよ]くなった。
After I studied Japanese, my interest in Japanese history became even stronger.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 に対する N2 "toward; for; in; with regard to" This grammar marks something to/toward/about which one does something, or mark someone to/toward whom one does something or owes something. In different contexts, it can mark something one has interest in. Do not confuse with the use where に対して indicates two contrasting actions, states, situations, etc."toward; for; in; with regard to" This grammar marks something to/toward/about which one does something, or mark someone to/toward whom one does something or owes something. In different contexts, it can mark something one has interest in. Do not confuse with the use where に対して indicates two contrasting actions, states, situations, etc.
番[ばん]港[こう]と 言[い]えば、 山[やま]の 上[うえ]から 見[み]る 夜[よる]の 景色[けしき]が 素晴[すば]らしい そうですね。
Speaking of Hong Kong, I hear that the view at night from the top of the hill (lit. mountain) is wonderful.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ~と言えば, which literally means "if you say that--," is used to present, as the topic, something or someone that has just been mentioned by the hearer or speaker. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Speaking of ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ X と言えば (X is usually a noun phrase)
京都[きょうと]と いう 町[まち]は、 古[ふる]い お寺[てら]が あるだけでなく、 日本[にほん]の 伝統[でんとう] 文化[ぶんか]の 中心[ちゅうしん] 地[ち]でも ある。
Kyoto is not only home to many ancient temples; it is also the center of traditional Japanese culture.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N／ANa でもある "be also" X は Y でもある. OR X は Y でもあり、Z でもある。 Are used to introduce another property of X when X has more than one property.
日本[にほん]の 伝統[でんとう] 芸能[げいのう]と いうのは、 つまり、 日本[にほん]の 昔[むかし]の コメディなんですね。
So, in other words, the Japanese traditional performing art kyogen is Japan's old (form of) comedy, right?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1/NP1, つまり、N2/NP2 "That is (to say); in other words; namely; (that) means; you mean ~?" つまりis used to rephrase or restate what has just been mentioned or stated.
奈良[なら]は 日本[にほん]で 一番[いちばん] 歴史[れきし]の 古[ふる]い 町[まち]の 一[ひと]つと 言[い]えるでしょう。
It probably can be said that Nara is one of the cities with the oldest histories in Japan.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This pattern is used when the speaker is quite certain that his/her statement is correct but wants to soften the statement so as not to appear too assertive. This is a formal expression. --- 英訳 [English translation]: It probably can be said that ~; it is probably all right to say that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S-plain と言えるだろう
京都[きょうと]や 奈良[なら]は 歴史[れきし]的[てき]な 建物[たてもの]が たくさん ある 伝統[でんとう]的[てき]な 街[まち]です。
Kyoto and Nara are traditional towns with many historic buildings.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N+的 the suffix is attached to nouns to make them な-adjectives. When these adj modify nouns, the な is sometimes omitted.
酸素[さんそ]や 水[みず]を 必要[ひつよう]と しない 生物[せいぶつ]は 地球[ちきゅう]には いない。
Every living being on earth needs oxygen and water.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V−nai ない N は{ない／いない} Means: There is no N which/who does not V This construction is used to create sentences containing double negatives. VないNは(い)ない is equivalent to "All Ns V."
大[おお]きいな 災害[さいがい]の 時[とき]は、 みんなで 助[たす]け合[あ]う ことが 大切[たいせつ]だ。
In the event of a big disaster, it is important that everyone help each other.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 合う, when combined with another verb, forms a compound verb, adding the meaning "to each other." --- 英訳 [English translation]: V (to/for) each other; V with~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V−masu合う: 話し合う; 見せ合う; 助け合う; 信じ合う
英語[えいご]の presidentに 当[あ]たる 言葉[ことば]は、 日本[にほん]語[ご]の 場合[ばあい]、 会社[かいしゃ]では 「社長[しゃちょう]」、 大学[だいがく]では 「学長[がくちょう]」、 米国[べいこく] 政府[せいふ]では 「大統領[だいとうりょう]」です。
In the case of Japanese, the words which correspond to the English word "president" is "しゃちょう” in a company, "がくちょう” in a University, and "だいとうりょう” for the American government.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

Yに当たるZはXだ。 X,Y,Z = nouns Means: The Z which is equivalent to Y is X; the Z which corresponds to Y is X. his grammar is often used to contrast words/phrases in two languages or organizations/professional titles in two countries.
15[じゅうご]年[ねん]も 飼[か]っていた 犬[いぬ]が、 年[とし]を 取[と]って とうとう 死[し]んでしまったので、 とても 悲[かな]しい。
I'm really sad because the dog I've had for 15 long years has finally died.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

とうとう V "finally; at (long) last; eventually; in the end; after all" とうとう indicates that an expected situation has occurred after an extended period of time. The adverb ついに is similar to とうとう and can be used in the place of とうとう. ついに is more formal.
東京[とうきょう]から 九州[きゅうしゅう]まで 新[しん]幹線[かんせん]で 行[い]くか 飛行[ひこう] 機[き]で 行[い]くか、 まだ 決[き]めていないんです。
I haven't decided yet whether I'm going to go from Tokyo to Kyushu by bullet train or by plane.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The phrase AかBか is used to present alternatives. When Bか is followed by a case particle (e.g., が, を, へ, に, で, と), the second か is usually dropped. --- 英訳 [English translation]: either A or B; whether A or B --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. 〜か〜か b. N1かN2+Particle
東京[とうきょう]から 京都[きょうと]に 行[い]くには、 新[しん]幹線[かんせん]が 早[はや]くて 便利[べんり]ですよ。
To get from Tokyo to Kyoto, the bullet train is a fast, convenient way.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past.aff には "to; in order to; for; for the purpose of; when" には indicates purpose in general statements (often stating the speaker's judgement about an action in terms of its effectiveness, convenience, necessity, etc.). には can also mean "when" (=時には). Verbs or nouns can precede には. Note that when ために is used, the predicate in the main clause describes an action. Such that: Xには Y, where Y is a judgment and never an action XためにY, where Y is an action and never a judgement. AND, XためにはY, where Y is a judgment, never an action
過去[かこ]に おいて、 その 問題[もんだい]に ついて だれも 対策[たいさく]を 考[かんが]えなかったと いう わけでは ない。
It is not that in the past no one has given a thought as to how to deal with the problem.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 において V "in;at;on;during" The compound particle における indicate the place or time of an action, event, or state. The pre-verbal form is において. Both are used only in formal language.

日本[にほん]の 義務[ぎむ] 教育[きょういく]は 小[しょう]学校[がっこう]が 6[ろく]年[ねん]、 中[ちゅう]学校[がっこう]が 3[さん]年[ねん]である。 一方[いっぽう] 私[わたし]の 組[く]んでは、 小[しょう]学校[がっこう]だけが 義務[ぎむ] 教育[きょういく]で、 中[ちゅう]学校[がっこう]から 入[はい]っても いかなくても いい。 しかし、 ほとんどの 子供[こども]たちは 中[ちゅう]学校[がっこう]に 進学[しんがく] (to go on to) する。

Compulsory education in Japan is made up of six years of elementary school and three of middle school. On the other hand, in my country only elementary school is compulsary, and schooling is optional from middle school on. Still, most students go on to middle school.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1 一方（で）、S2. "While; when; at the same time; on the other hand" The conjunction 一方 is used to present two contrastive situations or two concurrent states, events or actions. 一方 is usually used in written language.
親[おや]が 立派[りっぱ]であればあるほど、 子供[こども]は プレッシャーを 感[かん]じてしまう ようだ。
The more prominent/splended parents are, the more pressure children feel.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{Ana/NP} であれば ({ANa/NP}で)あるほど "the (more) ~, the (more) ~" This structure is used when the more something happens or is in some state, the more another thing happens or is in some state. (In this case, it appears that Ana in this structure do not need to be restated before ほど)
日本[にほん]語[ご]は、 話[はな]せる ことは 話[はな]せるが、 通訳[つうやく]が できるほどでは ない。
I can speak Japanese alright, but not well enough to act as an interpreter.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past ほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb.
日本[にほん]では 秋[あき]に なると 仕事[しごと]の 面接[めんせつ]に 行[い]く スーツ 姿[すがた]の 学生[がくせい]が 増[ふ]える。
When fall comes in Japan, you start to see more students in suits on their way to job interviews.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (の）姿 "in ~; wearing ~; 姿 means "appearance; figure". It is used to describe someone's external appearance, i.e. someone's form or physical form or physical appearance; someone's appearance in certain clothing; or the ay someone appears when he/she is doing something.
現代[げんだい]の 日本[にほん]の 女性[じょせい]の 姿[すがた]を 見[み]ていると、 女性[じょせい]は 本当[ほんとう]に 強[つよ]くなったなあと 思[おも]う。
Looking at women in Japan today, I feel like they've really become strong.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (の）姿 "in ~; wearing ~; 姿 means "appearance; figure". It is used to describe someone's external appearance, i.e. someone's form or physical form or physical appearance; someone's appearance in certain clothing; or the ay someone appears when he/she is doing something.
トムさんは 日本[にほん]食[しょく]が 大好[だいす]きだ そうだ。 納豆[なっとう]さえ 食[た]べるらしい。
I heard Tom loves Japanese food. Apparently he even eats natto.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (prt) さえ Means: even さえ is an emphatic particle. In non-conditional clauses it means "even." When さえ is used, the particle が never occurs, を usually does not occur, へ and the directional に are optional, and the other particles, including the LOCATIONAL に, で、と and から are mandatory.
会議[かいぎ]で 決[き]まった ことに 従[したが]って プロジェクトを 進[すす]めてください。
Please carry this project forward in accordance with what was decided at the meeting.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
〜に従って literally means "following." In some contexts, it means "in accordance with" or "complying with"
子供[こども]たちの 学力[がくりょく]が 低下[ていか] する 一方[いっぽう]で、 受験[じゅけん] 戦争[せんそう]は ますます 激[はげ]しくなっている。
While children's academic skills decline, the entrance exam wars become more and more fierce.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1 一方（で）、S2. "While; when; at the same time; on the other hand" The conjunction 一方 is used to present two contrastive situations or two concurrent states, events or actions. 一方 is usually used in written language.
奈良[なら]は 京都[きょうと]と 並[なら]んで、 古[ふる]い 歴史[れきし]の ある 町[まち]で、 日本[にほん]の 首都[しゅと]だった ことも ある。
Nara, like Kyoto, is a city with a long history and used to be the capital of Japan.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N と並んで "as well as; just like" Is used when introducing one or more examples to be compared to the subject of the sentence. It is used primarily in written language.
9.11[きゅうてんいちいち] 以来[いらい]、 飛行[ひこう] 機[き]に 乗[の]る ときの セキュリティ チェックが とても 厳[きび]しくなった。
Since 9/11, security checks at airports have become extremely strict.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-te 以来 "since" It is used with V-te or VN referring to an action in the past, or with N indicating a specific time in the past.
友達[ともだち]の 誕生[たんじょう] 日[び]に プレゼントを 送[おく]りたいんだけど、 何[なに]が いいと 思[おも]う？
I want to send my friend a present for (her) birthday. What do you think is good?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: S んだけど／ですが is used as a preliminary remark by the speaker to inform the hearer of the speaker's desire, the current situation, etc. before (a) asking a question related to that desire, (b) asking for an opinion on the matter, or (c) making a request. This phrase can also be used to extend an invitation or an offer. When making a request, the request is often unstated, as shown below. んだけど is more casual than んですが. --- 英訳 [English translation]: but (in english, null in most situations) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜ん{だけど/ですが}
A) 昨日[きのう]、 友達[ともだち]の 誕生[たんじょう] 日[び] パーティに 行[い]ってきたんだ。 B） あっ、 そう いえば、 明日[あした]は 母[はは]の 誕生[たんじょう] 日[び]だ。 忘[わす]れてた！
A) I went to my friend's birthday party yesterday. B) Ah, that reminds me that tomorrow's my mother's birthday. I forgot!
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
そう言えば Means: That reminds me; Now i remember; indeed This conjunctive phrase is used when the speaker is reminded of something by the hearer's remark or the speaker's own remark.
日本[にほん]で 働[はたら]きたいのなら、 日本[にほん]の 会社[かいしゃ]に 就職[しゅうしょく] できる ように、 日本[にほん]語[ご]を もっと 練習[れんしゅう] しておいた 方[ほう]が いいですよ。
If you want to work in Japan, so you should practice your Japanese harder so that you can get a job at a Japanese company.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) This construction is used to state either a purpose or the way in which something is to be done. In XようにY, X represents a state or event which is beyond the control of the subject of Y. The verb form before ように is often a potential form or a negative form. (2) In the similar construction XためにY, X represents an action which can be controlled by the subject of Y, while XようにY implies that a certain consequence (X) will arise as the result of an action (Y). --- 英訳 [English translation]: so that ~; in such a way that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.nonpastように
就職[しゅうしょく] しようか、 あるいは、 大学[だいがく]院[いん]に 進[すす]んで 勉強[べんきょう]を 続[つづ]けようか、 今[いま]、 迷[まよ]っている。
Right now I'm torn between looking for work and going on to graduate school to continue my studies.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S1 か、あるいは、S２ か "or; either ~ or ~" あるいは is used to connect alternatives. It is usually used in formal speech or written language.
これは アメリカに就[つ]いての 本[ほん]だが、 英語[えいご]では なく、 スペイン語[ご]で 書[か]かれている。
This is a book about the US, but it's written in Spanish, not English.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate that a certain piece of information is wrong and, following that, to present the correct information. ではなく(て) is used in written language and じゃなく(て) is used in spoken language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: not A, but B --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 {では/じゃ}なく(て) N2 b. Phrase1 {では/じゃ}なく(て) Phrase2
母[はは]が 病気[びょうき]で 苦[くる]しむ 姿[すがた]を 見[み]て、 私[わたし]は 将来[しょうらい] 医者[いしゃ]に なろうと 心[こころ]に 決[き]めた。
As I watched my mother suffering from her illness, I determined to myself that I would become a doctor in the future.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past 姿 "the way one V" 姿 means "appearance; figure". It is used to describe someone's external appearance, i.e. someone's form or physical form or physical appearance; someone's appearance in certain clothing; or the ay someone appears when he/she is doing something.
先生[せんせい]の アドバイスに 従[したが]って 勉強[べんきょう] したら、 成績[せいせき]が よくなった。
When I studied in the way my teacher suggested, my grades got better.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
〜に従って literally means "following." In some contexts, it means "in accordance with" or "complying with"
カタカナは 外国[がいこく]から 日本[にほん]に 入[はい]ってきた 言葉[ことば]や、 動物[どうぶつ]、 桜[さくら]の 名前[なまえ]など、 特別[とくべつ]な 名詞[めいし]に 使[つか]われます。 一方[いっぽう]、 ひらがなは、 助詞[じょし]や 文末[ぶんまつ]、 送[おく]り仮名[がな]などに 使[つか]われる ことが 多[おお]いです。

Katakana is used to write foreign loan words and certain nounds such as animal and flower names. Hiragana, on the other hand, is used mostly for particles, sentence endings, and okurigana (i.e., hiragara that follow kanji when they represent a single word, as in 大きい).
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1 一方（で）、S2. "While; when; at the same time; on the other hand" The conjunction 一方 is used to present two contrastive situations or two concurrent states, events or actions. 一方 is usually used in written language.
私[わたし]の アパートでは、 ペットを 飼[か]っては いけない ことに なっています。
It is a rule at my apartment that you cannot keep pets.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.non-past ことになっている means that something has been decided and the result of the decision is still in effect. It is often used to introduce rules or customs, as well as one's schedule. --- 英訳 [English translation]: be supposed to ~; It is a rule that ~; It's been decided that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-past ことになっている: {行く/行かない}ことになっている
北海道[ほっかいどう]から 沖縄[おきなわ]に 至[いた]るまで、 同[おな]じ 時代[じだい]に 同[おな]じ NHK ニュースが 見[み]られます。
You can see the same NHK news at the same time from Hokkaido all the way to Okinawa.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 から N2 に至まで "from N1 all the way through N2; from N1 to even N2." This construction indicates a span of time or space and emphasizes the size of that span at the same time. It can also be used for other than spatial or temporal spans, as seen here. Primarily used in written language.
お宅[たく]の 聖地[せいち]、 すなわち、 東京[とうきょう]の 秋葉原[あきはばら]は、 電気[でんき] 製品[せいひん]が 安[やす]い 「電気[でんき]の 町[まち]」でも ある。
The otaku "holy land", i.e. Akihabara in Tokyo, is also an "Electric Town", where you can get electronic goods cheaply.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
NP1/S1, すなわち NP2/S2 "that is; i.e.; namely" すなわち
聖徳[しょうとく] 太子[たいし] (Prince Shotaku)と いう 人物[じんぶつ]は、 一度[いちど]に 十[じゅう]人[にん]の 人[ひと]が 話[はな]している ことが 分[わ]かったと いう。
They say that Prince Shotaku could listen to eight people talking at once and understand all of them.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain という "It is said that ~; They say that ~" This structure indicate that the preceding information is not first hand. This is a polite form.
兄[あに]は 自分[じぶん]で 料理[りょうり] しない くせに、 いつも 私[わたし]の 作[つく]った ものに 文句[もんく]を 言[い]う。
My older brother doesn't cook (himself) and yet he always complains about what I make.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

〜くせに Means: Although~; in spite of the fact that~; and yet~ This conjunction is used when something commonly expected from information in the subordinate clause (i.e. the くせに phrase/clause) does not happen or is not the case. In most situations, くせに expresses the speaker's anger, frustration or disagreement. This emotion is not directed toward the speaker, but toward the hearer or 3rd person. When くせに is used, the subject of the main clause and that of the subordinate clause must be the same. If the subjects differ, you must use なのに、.
日本[にほん]語[ご]の 授業[じゅぎょう]で、 日本[にほん]には 宗教[しゅうきょう]的[てき] 習慣[しゅうかん]や 行事[ぎょうじ]は たくさん あるが、 宗教[しゅうきょう]に 熱心[ねっしん]な 信者[しんじゃ]は あまり いないと いう ことを 学[まな]んだ。
In Japanese class, we learned that in Japan there are a lot of religious customs and events, but not many fervent believers in religion.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S-plain ということ(が、を、etc) General meaning: that; V-ing changes a sentence into a noun clause, but does not add any meaning. The noun clause can be marked by が、を, etc. This phrase is usually used in WRITTEN language.
宗教[しゅうきょう]の 問題[もんだい]が 理[り] 解決[かいけつ] しない 限[かぎ]り、 おそらく この 戦争[せんそう]は 終[お]わらないだろう。
As long as the religious problems remain unresolved, it's unlikely that this war will end.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
おそらく〜だろう "probably" おそらく means "probably" and usually occurs with the conjecture auxiliaries だろう or でしょう。
昨日[きのう]から 頭[あたま]が 痛[いた]くて しかたが ない。 眼鏡[めがね]が 合[あ]わないのかも しれない。
I've had a terrible headache since yesterday. Maybe my glasses aren't good.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{A/v}-te しかたがない／しようがない／しょうがない "cannot help V-ing; cannot stop feeling ~; so ~; unbearably ~" てしかたない、てしようがない,etc. literally mean that a situation is such or is occurring and there is no way to escape it. The phrases are used to indicate that the speaker is unable to control his psychological/physiological reactions or bear a sensation or an external situation. しょうがない i s the colloquial version. This use is different from the following example, where the しかたがない means "it cannot be helped; there's nothing one can do." お金がないのだから、留学できないのはしかたがない。
この 政治[せいじ]家[か]って、 衆議[しゅうぎ]院[いん]だったっけ。 参議[さんぎ]院[いん]だったっけ？
This politician - is he in the House of Representatives or the House of Councilors?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{ANa/N/QW} だった (んだ) っけ っけ is a question marker used in very casual conversation. Note that after the non-past forms of V, A and ~ない, んだ must be used before っけ。
自由[じゆう]と 独立[どくりつ]と いう 教[おし]えを もとに その 憲法[けんぽう]が 作[つく]られた。
That constitution was created based on the concepts of freedom and independence.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: をもとにして is a compound particle meaning "based on."して here is optional. The noun-modification form is をもとにした. --- 英訳 [English translation]: based on --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nをもとに(して) N1をもとにしたN2
俳句[はいく]だけでなく、 単価[たんか]も また 日本[にほん]を 代表[だいひょう] する 文字[もじ]の 一[ひと]つと して 知[し]られている。
In addition to haiku, tanka is also well known as a literary style representative of Japan.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
もまた "as well; also; too" In this usage もまた means the same as も; however it is more emphatic and formal than も.
この サイトは 携帯[けいたい] 電話[でんわ]向[む]けだから、 コンピュータでは 見[み]にくい。
This site was made for cell phones, so its hard to see on the computer.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N 向けだ Means: for; made for; for the use of; directed to The suffix 向け adds the meaning "made for; for the use of; directed toward." 向け is often affixed to nouns which refer to people, countries and organizations.
この 携帯[けいたい] 電話[でんわ]の コマーシャルは なかなか 面白[おもしろ]い。
This cell phone commercial is pretty interesting.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

なかなか (A/ANa+だ) Means: quite; fairly; pretty; considerably なかなか is synonymous with 結構 except that なかなか is NOT usually used with adj and adv with negative meanings, such as つまらない or 不便. Note that なかなか is used with the speaker is impressed by the way something/someone is or the way someone does something.
この 携帯[けいたい] 電話[でんわ]は、 電話[でんわ]を するだけでなく、 カメラと しても 使[つか]える。
Not only can you use this cell phone to make calls, you can also use it as a camera.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: として is used to indicate the role, capacity, or occupation of someone or the function or characteristics of something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: as; in the capacity of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nとして
友達[ともだち]の 携帯[けいたい]に 電話[でんわ]を かけている ところに その 友達[ともだち]が 現[あらわ]れたので、 びっくり した。
I was surprised because my friend showed up just as I was calling her on her cell phone.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V−teいるところ Means: (when)~ is V-ing; (while)~is V-ing; (when)~ is in the midst of V-ing ところ indicates a point in time just before, during, or just after an event, the time indicated depends on the preceding verb tense.
電車[でんしゃ]の 中[なか]や 病院[びょういん]などでは、 携帯[けいたい] 電話[でんわ]を 使[つか]うべきでは ない。
You shouldn't use your cell phone on the train or at the hospital.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V. plain.non-past.aff べき {だ／じゃない／ではない／だった／じゃなかった／ではなかった} "should; ought to" The auxillary べき expresses the speaker's strong judgment that one should do something. The form of する before べき can be either す or する, as in すべき or するべき。
コンピュータの 普及[ふきゅう]と 共[とも]に、 E メールを 使[つか]う 人[ひと]が 増[ふ]えた。
As computers became widespread, the number of people using e-mail increased.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Nと共に "with; along with; as" indicates that someone does something or that something happens with N.
教育[きょういく] 問題[もんだい]に 対[たい]する この 国[くに]の 対策[たいさく]は 全[まった]く 間違[まちが]っていると 思[おも]う。
I think the measures this country is taking to deal with its educational problems are way off track.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

まったく {V/A/ANo/(の)N/Ano} "totally; utterly; entirely; completely; extremely; absolutely; really" used for emphasis in affirmative sentences. often used to express the speaker's emotion. In negative sentences, it indicates complete negation. It is used with verbs (often in potential form) and i-adjectives in negative sentences. まったく〜（という）わけではない indicates partial negation.
日本[にほん]語[ご]を 撮[と]っている 学生[がくせい]の うち、 30[さんじゅう]％ぐらいは 工学[こうがく] 部[ぶ]の 学生[がくせい]だ そうです。
I heard that about 30% of the students taking Japanese are engineering majors.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N のうち(で) "in; of; among" Xのうち(で）is used to indicate the total entity (X) when presenting a part or portion of X.
高校[こうこう]生[せい]の 時[とき]、 よく 友達[ともだち]と 写真[しゃしん]を 撮[と]り合[あ]ったり 見[み]せ合[あ]ったり して 遊[あそ]んだ。
When I was in high school, my friends and I used to take pictures of each other and show them to each other for fun.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 合う, when combined with another verb, forms a compound verb, adding the meaning "to each other." --- 英訳 [English translation]: V (to/for) each other; V with~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V−masu合う: 話し合う; 見せ合う; 助け合う; 信じ合う
最近[さいきん]の ケータイは 写真[しゃしん]が 撮[と]れるだけでなく、 メールも できる。 その 上[うえ]、 インターネットや テレビも 見[み]られる。 これは、 もう 電話[でんわ]じゃない。
The recent cell phones let you not only take pictures, but send e-mail too. On top of that, you can also access the Internet and watch TV. This is not a phone anymore.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1. その上、S2. Means: on top of that; in addition (to that); what's more; besides; moreover その上 is used when the speaker wants to emphasize an additional piece of information. S2 usually contains the particle も or まで。 as here.
私[わたし]の 母[はは]は、 未[いま]だに 携帯[けいたい] 電話[でんわ]を 持[も]たずに 生活[せいかつ] している。
My mother still lives without having a cell phone.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
未だに "still; (not ~) yet" indicates that someone of something is in the same state as he/she/it was some time ago. This form is primarily used in written language. In spoken language まだ is used.
風[かぜ]の 予報[よほう]には、 ビタミン Cを たくさん 撮[と]って、 よく 寝[ね]るのが 結果[けっか]的[てき]です。
Gettings lots of vitamin C and plenty of sleep is effective in preventing colds.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (of a VN, or direct object of する) には "to; in order to; for; for the purpose of; when" には indicates purpose in general statements (often stating the speaker's judgement about an action in terms of its effectiveness, convenience, necessity, etc.). には can also mean "when" (=時には). Verbs or nouns can precede には. Note that when ために is used, the predicate in the main clause describes an action. Such that: Xには Y, where Y is a judgment and never an action XためにY, where Y is an action and never a judgement. AND, XためにはY, where Y is a judgment, never an action
田中[たなか]君[くん]は 僕[ぼく]たちと 同[おな]じぐらいの 年[とし]だと 思[おも]うよ。
I think Tanaka-kun is about the same age as we are.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The particle ぐらい/くらい "approximately" often occurs with 同じ to mean "about the same." --- 英訳 [English translation]: about as ~ as; about the same ~ as ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N と同じ{ぐらい/くらい} b. N1 と同じ{ぐらい/くらい}の N2
それは、 僕[ぼく]には 関係[かんけい]が ないから、 知[し]らないなあ。
That is not related to me, so I don't know about it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 は N2 {と／に}関係がある。 This sentence is used to show that N1 is related in someway to N2. The particle after N1 may be と or に。 When this pattern is used in relative clauses, の is commonly used after 関係 instead of が。
ポチは 僕[ぼく]が 大学[だいがく]に 入[はい]る 前[まえ]は まだ 子供[こども]だったのに、 休[やす]みに 家[いえ]に 帰[かえ]る たびに、 どんどん 大[おお]きくなっている。
Before I went off to college, Pochi was still just a puppy, but every time I come home for break he's gotten so much bigger.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past たびに "every time; each time; on every ~; whenever" たびに expresses the idea that each time someone does something, something else takes place. When たびに is modified by a noun, the noun refers to an action or certain time.
僕[ぼく]の 身長[しんちょう]は 6[ろく]フィート、 メートル 法[ほう]で 言[い]うと 約[やく]180[ひゃくはちじゅう]センチだ。
I'm 6 feet tall or, going by the metric system, around 180 centimeters.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

"in terms of; in; according to; from the viewpoint of" で言うと is used to restate something according to a different system or framework (e.g. a calendar, a measurement system, a language, a country's history)
加藤[かとう] 先生[せんせい]は 大学[だいがく]院[いん]の 時[とき]に 書[か]いた 論文[ろんぶん]を もとに 本[ほん]を 書[か]きました。
Professor Kato wrote a book based on a thesis he wrote when he was in graduate school.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: をもとにして is a compound particle meaning "based on."して here is optional. The noun-modification form is をもとにした. --- 英訳 [English translation]: based on --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nをもとに(して) N1をもとにしたN2
彼[かれ]が 私[わたし]を 好[す]きだと いう ことは、 彼[かれ]の 友達[ともだち]を 通[とお]して 聴[き]いた。 とても うれしかった。
It was from one of his friends that I heard that he likes me, which made me very happy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N を通して "through; via" を通して indicates a medium (X) through which someone does something or something happens. X can be things, people, activities or actions.
トムさんは 日本[にほん]語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]な ため、 ときどき 通訳[つうやく]を 頼[たの]まれる。
Due to Tom being good at Japanese, he is sometimes asked to be an interpreter.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by an i-adjective or a na-adjective or the past form of a verb, it indicates reason or cause. When it is preceded by the non-past form of a verb or a noun, it means either reason/cause or purpose. The meaning is determined from the context. Whenため(に) means reason/cause, it can be replaced by 〜から or 〜ので, which are less formal than 〜ために. --- 英訳 [English translation]: because; due to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {この/その/あの}ため(に)
僕[ぼく]の 名前[なまえ]は 「つとむ」だけど、 友達[ともだち]は 「トム」って 呼[よ]ぶんだ。
My name is "tsutomu," but my friends call me "tom."
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: って is the informal colloquial form of the quotative marker と. って commonly occurs with verbs like 言う, 聞く, 書く and 呼ぶ. --- 英訳 [English translation]: (tell, hear, say, etc.) that ~ Noun1っていうNoun2 = Noun2 called Noun1 --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Sって{言う/聞く/書く} b. Nって{言う/聞く/呼ぶ} c. N1っていうN2
ほら、 あと 1[いち]キロで ゴールだよ。 頑張[がんば]れ！
Come on, there's only one more kilometer to the goal! Hang in there!
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ほら "Look!; See?; Come on!" The interjection ほら can be used to draw the hearer's attention to something. Only used in very casual conversation.
練習[れんしゅう] すれば、 もっと 上手[じょうず]に 話[はな]せる ようになっていくよ。 頑張[がんば]ってね。
If you practice, you'll get even better at speaking. Good luck!
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-teくる and V-teいく indicate the temporal or spatial direction of an action from the speaker's viewpoint. V-teくる is used when an action appears to be directed toward the speaker, and V-teいく is used when it appears to be directed away from the speaker. V-teくる often indicates that an action or process began in the past and is continuing in the present, or that something has begun to take place. V-teいく, on the other hand, often expresses an action or state that will continue from the present into the future. In other uses, 来る and 行くfollowing V-te maintain their original meanings, i.e., "to come" and "to go." --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-teくる = have V-ed; begin to; become; grow V−teいく = go on V-ing; continue; become; grow --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te来る/行く
スミス 先生[せんせい]は、 僕[ぼく]の 日本[にほん]語[ご]の 先生[せんせい]である 森[もり] 先生[せんせい]を 知[し]っておられる そうだ。
I heard that Prof. Smith knows Prof. Mori, my Japanese teacher.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-te いる: V-te おられる Passive forms of verbs are used to indicate politeness when the speaker refers to the actions of the hearer or someone to whom the speaker wants to show deference. However, this use of passive forms does not indicate as high a level of politeness as おV-masu になる or special honorific verbs like いらっしゃる and めし上がる。 Note that the polite form of the auxilliary verb いる is not いられる, but おられる. The auxilliary verb おられる is less polite than いらっしゃる。
子犬[こいぬ]が 寝[ね]ている ところを 写真[しゃしん]に 撮[と]った。 とても かわいい 写真[しゃしん]が 撮[と]れた。
I took a picture of the puppy napping. I could take a very cute picture.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V−teいるところ Means: (when)~ is V-ing; (while)~is V-ing; (when)~ is in the midst of V-ing ところ indicates a point in time just before, during, or just after an event, the time indicated depends on the preceding verb tense.
僕[ぼく]の 犬[いぬ]は 散歩[さんぽ]に 連[つ]れて行[い]くと、 ちょっと 歩[ある]いては 立[た]ち留[ど]まって 花[はな]を クンクン させ、 なかなか 前[まえ]に 進[すす]まない。
When I take my dog for a walk, he stops every few feet, sniffing this and that, and it's hard to move on.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V1-te は V2 "V1 and V2 repeatedly/over and over again/many times/etc." The construction of VteはV is used when a set of actions is repeated over a period of time. It can be said once, or repeated, as here.
田中[たなか]さんの 嫌[きら]いな 食[た]べ物[もの]って 何[なん]?
What foods don't you like, Mr. Tanaka?/What foods doesn't Mr. Tanaka like?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: って is a colloquial topic marker. It often appears in questions. In written language, は can be used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Speaking of ~, As for ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N って
あの 人[ひと]が 嫌[きら]いな わけでは ないんですが、 デート したいとは 思[おも]いません。
It's not that I dislike that person, I don't think I want to date (him/her).
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ANa {な／だった／じゃない／じゃなかった} わけではない Means: It's not that~; It doesn't mean that used to deny a statement.
今日[きょう]は 朝[あさ]から、 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]っては やみ、 降[ふ]っては やみ していて 嫌[いや]な 天気[てんき]だ。
The weather's horrible today; it's been raining off and on since this morning.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V1-te は V2 "V1 and V2 repeatedly/over and over again/many times/etc." The construction of VteはV is used when a set of actions is repeated over a period of time. It can be said once, or repeated, as here.
これは なかなか 上手[じょうず]に 描[えが]けたと 思[おも]う。
I think this was drawn quite well.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

なかなか Adv Means: quite; fairly; pretty; considerably なかなか is synonymous with 結構 except that なかなか is NOT usually used with adj and adv with negative meanings, such as つまらない or 不便. Note that なかなか is used with the speaker is impressed by the way something/someone is or the way someone does something
私[わたし]は 絵[え]を 描[えが]くのは 得意[とくい]じゃないけれど、 これは なかなか 上手[じょうず]に 描[えが]けたと 思[おも]う。
I'm not very good at painting, but I think this turned out fairly well.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

なかなか (A/ANa+だ) Means: quite; fairly; pretty; considerably なかなか is synonymous with 結構 except that なかなか is NOT usually used with adj and adv with negative meanings, such as つまらない or 不便. Note that なかなか is used with the speaker is impressed by the way something/someone is or the way someone does something.
この 絵[え]は モネに よって 描[えが]かれたと されているが、 絵[え]の 中[なか]に モネの サインは 入[はい]っていない。
This painting is believed to have been painted by Monet, but his signature doesn't appear on the canvas.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain とされている "it is thought/believed/considered that~; ~ is considered/believed to ~" This is used to introduce a commonly accepted idea or belief.
納豆[なっとう]は 嫌[きら]いだが、 まったく 食[た]べられないと いう わけでは ない。
I don't like natto, but it's not that I can't eat it at all.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

まったく〜（という）わけではない "It's not that ~ totally/completely/extremely/etc." used for emphasis in affirmative sentences. often used to express the speaker's emotion. In negative sentences, it indicates complete negation. It is used with verbs (often in potential form) and i-adjectives in negative sentences. まったく〜（という）わけではない indicates partial negation.
週末[しゅうまつ]は 宿題[しゅくだい]が 沢山[たくさん] あったので、 勉強[べんきょう]の 他(に)[ほか]は 何[なに]も 出来[でき]なかった。
I had a lot of homework over the weekend, so I couldn't do anything other than study.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Nの他に(も) is an adverbial phrase meaning "in addition to N." Verbs, adjectives and demonstrative adjectives can also precede 他に(も) to mean "in addition to V-ing," "in addition to being Adj." or "in addition to this/that." ~他(に)は also means "in addition to." In some contexts, the phrase can mean "except for; other than" --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~他に(も) = in addition to ~; besides ~他(に)は(~ない) = (not ~) except for ~; (not~) other than ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~他に(も); ~他(に)は {この/その/あの}他に(も)
何[なん]歳[さい]で 運転[うんてん] 免許[めんきょ]が 取[と]れるかは、 国[くに]に よって 違[ちが]う ようです。
It seems that the age at which you can get your driver's license differs depending on the country.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate that something differs depending on the situation, location, time, etc. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~によって違う = differ depending on ~ / due to ~ による = depend on, due to, according to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {Noun/Question Word ~ か/ ~かどうか}は Noun に {よって違う / よる }
去年[きょねん] 佐藤[さとう]さんと 来[き]た 日本[にほん] 料理[りょうり]の レストランは、 ここじゃなかったかなあ。
This doesn't look like the Japanese restaurant I came to with Sato-san last year, but I'm not sure.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 〜かなあ is a sentence final particle which indicates that the sentence is a self-addressed question or a question addressed to the speaker's in-group member(s). It is used only in casual language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: I wonder ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜かな(あ)
インスタント ラーメンを 作[つく]り出[だ]したのは、 安藤[あんどう] 百福[ももふく]と いう 人[ひと]です。
The inventor of instant ramen is a man named Ando Momofuku.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-masu 出す Means: V out; begin to V; start to V; begin V-ing; start V-ing V出す differs from V始める in that V出す is used for abrupt and non-volitional actions, while V始める is used for both volitional and non-volitional actions but NOT for actions which begin abruptly. V-masu 出す has 2 meanings, here is the (2) Someone begins something or something begins
携帯[けいたい] 電話[でんわ]が なかった ころは、 よく 友達[ともだち]を 待[ま]たせたり、 逆[ぎゃく]に 待[ま]たせられたり した ものだが、 今[いま]は すぐ 連絡[れんらく] できるので とても 便利[べんり]だ。

Back before there were cell phones, it often happened that I caused my friends to wait for me or my friends caused me to wait for them, but now we can get in touch right away, so it's really convenient.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-plain.non-past ものだ "used to ~; would" V-plain.past ものだ is used to describe in a nostalgic fashion what someone did or what happened in the past
留学[りゅうがく]中[ちゅう]、 沖縄[おきなわ]を 除[のぞ]く 日本[にほん] 全国[ぜんこく] 各地[かくち]を 友達[ともだち]と 一緒[いっしょ]に 旅行[りょこう] した。
WhileI was studying in Japan, I travelled everywhere but Okinawa.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 を除く N2 "except (for); with the exception of ~; but ~" 除く means "to remove; get rid of." を除いて is used as a compound particle meaning "except."
彼[かれ]は ギターが とても 上手[じょうず]だ。 どんな 曲[きょく]でも 弾[ひ]ける。
He is skilled at playing guitar. No matter what tune it is, he can play it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ても is used with a question word, the phrase means: "no matter" or "without regard to." --- 英訳 [English translation]: no matter what/who/when/where/how --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ QW(prt)+V-teも
ファースト フードの 特徴[とくちょう]は いろいろ あるが、 まず、 速[はや]くて 安[やす]いと いう ことが 言[い]えるだろう。
Fast food has a variety of characteristics. First, we can say that it is quick and cheap.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S-plain ということ(が、を、etc) General meaning: that; V-ing changes a sentence into a noun clause, but does not add any meaning. The noun clause can be marked by が、を, etc. This phrase is usually used in WRITTEN language.
プラスチックが 持[も]つ 様々[さまざま]な 特徴[とくちょう]は、 多[おお]くの 製品[せいひん]の 中[なか]で 生[い]かされている。
Many products make use of the various unique characteristics of plastic.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
生かす "make the most of; make the best use of; use effectively; maintain" 生かす means literally "to keep alive," but it is also used to mean "to make the most of one's ability, etc"
いつ 起[お]きるか 分[わ]からない 地震[じしん]に 対[たい]して、 対策[たいさく]を 考[かんが]えておかなければならない。
We need to think about how to deal with earthquakes, which are unpredictable as to when they will be hit.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N に対して "toward; for; in; with regard to" This grammar marks something to/toward/about which one does something, or mark someone to/toward whom one does something or owes something. In different contexts, it can mark something one has interest in. Do not confuse with the use where に対して indicates two contrasting actions, states, situations, etc.
コンピュータが 壊[こわ]れた ために、 レポートが 書[か]きませんでした。
Because my computer broke, I didn't write my report.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by an i-adjective or a na-adjective or the past form of a verb, it indicates reason or cause. When it is preceded by the non-past form of a verb or a noun, it means either reason/cause or purpose. The meaning is determined from the context. Whenため(に) means reason/cause, it can be replaced by 〜から or 〜ので, which are less formal than 〜ために. --- 英訳 [English translation]: because; due to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {この/その/あの}ため(に)
大[おお]きい 音[おと]に 驚[おどろ]いて、 ガムを 飲[の]み込[こ]んでしまった。
Surprised by a loud sound, I gulped down (swallowed deeply) my gum.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V−masu 込む "in; into; deeply; heavily; thoroughly; completely" The compound verb base 込む can mean one of 4 things: (A) Taking or putting something/someone into something {飲み込む}
よく 勉強[べんきょう] したんだから、 １００[ひゃく]点[てん]を 取[と]っても、 驚[おどろ]く こと ないよ。
You studied hard, so you shouldn't be surprised that you got a perfect score.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-plain.non-past すること（は）ない "don't have to ~; don't need to ~; It's not necessary to ~; There is no need to ~" In casual conversation the は may drop.
フォト ショップを 使[つか]うと、 写真[しゃしん]の 編集[へんしゅう]が 驚[おどろ]くほど 簡単[かんたん]にできる。
It's surprisingly easy to edit photos when you use Photoshop.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past ほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb.
驚[おどろ]いた ことに、 この 鳥[とり]は 人間[にんげん]の 言葉[ことば]が 話[はな]せるらしい。
To my surprise, it seems that this bird can speak human language.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain ことに “It is~ that~; I am/We are ~ that ~; To my ~" ことに is used to express the speaker's feeling or subjective judgment about what is said in the main clause. ことに can only be used with a limited set of words.
地球[ちきゅう]や 火星[かせい]、 木星[もくせい]、 金星[きんせい]などの 惑星[わくせい]は、 太陽[たいよう]を 中心[ちゅうしん]と して回[まわ]っている
The planets Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, etc. go around their center, the sun.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N を 中心 {と/に} (して） "(centering) around; focusing on; mainly; with N as the center/focus/leader/etc." Nを中心(と/に)する literally means "to make N the center." This phrase takes 2 forms. The form used here is used to modify verbs. The phrase indicates that something takes place around N or with N as the center/focus, or that someone does something focusing on N.
子[こ] 農業[のうぎょう]で いい 成績[せいせき]が 撮[と]れるか どうかは、 期末[きまつ]の レポート 次第[しだい]だ。
Whether I get a good grade in this class or not depends on my final paper.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N次第だ "depend on N" When 次第 is affixed to nouns, it means "depend on."
兄[あに]は 長[なが]い 間[あいだ] 頑張[がんば]ってきたが、 ついに プロの フットボール 選手[せんしゅ]に なる 夢[ゆめ]を あきらめた。
My older brother gave it his best for years and years, but in the end he gave up on his dream of becoming a pro-football player.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The adverb ついに indicates that something happens or something expected doesn't happen, after waiting for it, longing for it, expecting it to happen, making an effort to make it happen, or after struggling/suffering in a hard situation for a long time. --- 英訳 [English translation]: at last; finally; in the end; after all --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ついに
兄[あに]と 違[ちが]い、 僕[ぼく]は スポーツが 余[あま]り 得意[とくい]じゃない。
Unlike my older brother, I'm not very good at sports.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The masu stem of a verb and the stem of an i-adjective + く indicate that the sentence is continuing. That is, they function like the English sentence connector "and." This use is generally restricted to written language. In spoken language the te-form of a verb or an i-adjective is commonly used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: and --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-masu、 ~ A-stem + く、 ~
風邪[かぜ]を 引[ひ]いた 時[とき]は ビタミン Cを 沢山[たくさん] 撮[と]るといいと 言[い]われている。
It is said that it's good to take lots of vitamin C when you get a cold.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to introduce something commonly said about something or someone. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~ it is said to be ~, It is said that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ーはSentence-plainと言われている
夕[ゆう]べ 隣[となり]の 人[ひと]が 真[ま]夜中[よなか]まで パーティーを していて うるさかったので、 全然[ぜんぜん] 寝[ね]られなかった。
Yesterday my neighbor had a party until late into the night, and it was so loud I couldn't sleep at all.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

真っX where X = adjective or Noun Means: very; pure; totally; right; mid- 真っAdj indicates the degree of something is very high or is at the highest level. 真っNoun indicates the center of a space or time span. The english translation of 真っ varies according to the word that follows it.
隣[となり]の 家[いえ]の パーテイが あまりに うるさかったので、 警察[けいさつ]を 連絡[れんらく] した。
The party next door was so loud that I called the police.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
あまりに（も）{A/Anaだ} "too; excessively; so" あまりに（も） indicates that the degree of something is excessively high. It is commonly used in formal language.
ここから 隣[となり]の 町[まち]に かけて、 スーパーや レストランが 並[なら]んでいるので、 道[みち]が とても 混[こ]む。
There are supermarkets and restaurants lined up along the road from here to the next town, so the road gets so crowded.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 から N2 にかけて "from N1 to N2" indicates a span of time or space and is used primarily in written language.
今度[こんど]、 隣[となり]の 土地[とち]に 新[あたら]しい ビルが 建[た]つので、 おそらく うるさくなるでしょう。
There's going to be a new building going up on the lot next door, so it'll probably get noisy around here.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
おそらく〜だろう "probably" おそらく means "probably" and usually occurs with the conjecture auxiliaries だろう or でしょう。
隣[となり]の 部屋[へや]の 音楽[おんがく]が 気[き]に なって しかたが ない。 ちょっと うるさすぎる。
I can't help being distracted by the music from the room next door. It's a little too loud.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-te しかたがない "cannot help V-ing; cannot stop feeling ~; so ~; unbearably ~" てしかたない、てしようがない,etc. literally mean that a situation is such or is occurring and there is no way to escape it. The phrases are used to indicate that the speaker is unable to control his psychological/physiological reactions or bear a sensation or an external situation. しかたがない and しようがない are interchangeable. This use is different from the following example, where the しかたがない means "it cannot be helped; there's nothing one can do." お金がないのだから、留学できないのはしかたがない。
パーティーを していたら、 隣[となり]の アパートの 人[ひと]に 静[しず]かにする ように 言[い]われてしまいました。
When we had the party, the people next door came over and told us to be quiet. (Indirect Quote)
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
30[さんじゅう]人[にん]も パーティに 誘[さそ]ったから、 10[じゅう]人[にん]ぐらいは 来[き]てくれるだろう。
I invited as many as 30 people to the party, so I imagine at least about 10 will come.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When the particle は follows a quantifier (i.e., a word such as 3本 or 少し), it adds the meaning "at least." だけは and ぐらいは (or くらいは) after a noun have the same meaning. --- 英訳 [English translation]: at least. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number (+ Counter) は b. N だけは c. N {ぐらい/くらい}は
日本[にほん]の 歴史[れきし]上[じょう]、 明治[めいじ] 維新[いしん]は 大[おお]きい 意味[いみ]を 持[も]っている。
The Meiji Restoration is very significant in Japanese history.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N 上 "in terms of; from the viewpoint of ~; as far as ~ is concerned; according to ~" Nの上で and N上 are used to indicate that the speaker's statement refers only to N. Commonly used in written language.
あまりに 便利[べんり]な 生活[せいかつ]は、 人間[にんげん]を 駄目[だめ]にすると 思[おも]う。
I think that too convenient a lifestyle spoils some people.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
あまりに（も）{Adv/ANa/A-stem く} "too; excessively; so" あまりに（も） indicates that the degree of something is excessively high. It is commonly used in formal language.
リサーチを 通[とお]して、 私[わたし]達[たち]が いかに エネルギーを 無駄[むだ]に 使[つか]っているかを 知[し]った。
Through this research, I've learned just how much energy we're wasting.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
いかに〜か "how; how much; in what way" This structure occurs as an embedded interrogative sentence, where いかに means "how (much)" or "in what way". This structure is commonly used in written language.
あの 映画[えいが]は 全[まった]く 面白[おもしろ]くなかった。 時間[じかん]の 無駄[むだ]だった。
There was absolutely nothing interesting about that movie. It was a waste of time.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

まったく〜ない "not ~ at all; not ~ in the least" used for emphasis in affirmative sentences. often used to express the speaker's emotion. In negative sentences, it indicates complete negation. It is used with verbs (often in potential form) and i-adjectives in negative sentences. まったく〜（という）わけではない indicates partial negation.
彼[かれ]は 思春[ししゅん] 期[き]に 入[はい]ってから、 親[おや]に すごく 反抗[はんこう] する ようになった。
Since he hit puberty, he's really started to rebel against his parents.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (time period) に {入り/入って (から)} "since N began; after N began" N に入る literally means "to enter N," but when N is a noun indicating a time period, the phrase means "N begins." The most common form is N に入り or N に入って（から), meaning "since/after N began."
「デスノート」と いう 漫画[まんが]は アニメ化[か]も ゲーム化[か]も されました。
The manga "Death Note" has been made into both an anime and a video game.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N+化する Meaning: -ize; make; become; change to 化する is a suffix and adds the meaning "-ization" to nouns and no-adjectives.説明 [explanation]: The suffix 化[か] is affixed to nouns and no-adjectives and adds the meaning of "-ization," as in "mechanization" and "digitization." --- 英訳 [English translation]: ～化する = ize; make; become; change to ～化する = ization; making ~; becoming ~; changing to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N + 化: 日本化; 専門化; 機械化 (mechanization); カタカナ化 b. NO-Adj + 化: 最適化 (optimization)
この 内容[ないよう]から すると、 この 漫画[まんが]は 子供[こども]向[む]けでは なく、 大人[おとな]向[む]けの マンガだろう。
Judging from its content, this is probably a manga written with adults, not children, in mind.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Nからすると "judging from~" Introduces the source or basis for the speaker's conjecture or judgment. The information can be of any sort including visual or verbal.
オゾン 層[そう]の 破壊[はかい]がが 地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]の 原因[げんいん]の 一[ひと]つだと されている。
It's thought that the destruction of the ozone layer is one of the causes of global warming.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain とされている "it is thought/believed/considered that~; ~ is considered/believed to ~" This is used to introduce a commonly accepted idea or belief.
先輩[せんぱい]に よると、 あの 先生[せんせい]の 授業[じゅぎょう]は 大変[たいへん]らしい。
According to my upperclassmen, it seems that teacher's lessons are really difficult.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
〜らしい。 means: Seem; apparently; I heard that~; it looks like Nによると。 Means: according to N
空手[くうしゅ] 部[ぶ]では、 先輩[せんぱい]に 言[い]われた 通[とお]りに しないと、 怒[おこ]られてしまう。
In karate club, if you don't do exactly as you're told by your upperclassmen, you will make them angry.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain 通り（に） "the way; as; exactly like; following; according to" When 通り is modified by a verb or noun, it means "the way; as someone does; as something indicates." 通り can also be used as a suffix, in which case 通り is directly affixed to nouns and the pronunciation changes from とおり to どおり。
先輩[せんぱい]、 まだ 来[こ]られないんですか。
You're not ready to leave yet, sempai?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

irr-verbs: される;（来=こられる) Passive forms of verbs are used to indicate politeness when the speaker refers to the actions of the hearer or someone to whom the speaker wants to show deference. However, this use of passive forms does not indicate as high a level of politeness as おV-masu になる or special honorific verbs like いらっしゃる and めし上がる。 Note that the polite form of the auxilliary verb いる is not いられる, but おられる. The auxilliary verb おられる is less polite than いらっしゃる。
先輩[せんぱい]の 意見[いけん]に 従[したが]って、 夏[なつ]は アルバイトを せずに、 クラスを 取[と]る ことに した。
Following my sempai's advice, I decided to take classes this summer instead of working.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
〜に従って literally means "following." In some contexts, it means "in accordance with" or "complying with"
日本[にほん]の スポーツ クラブの 先輩[せんぱい]と 後輩[こうはい]の 関係[かんけい]って 面白[おもしろ]いね。 山田[やまだ]： うん、 ああ いう 関係[かんけい]って、 他[た]の 国[くに]では あまり 見[み]られないだろうね。
The senpai/kohai relationship in Japanese sports club is interesting, isn't it? Yamada: yeah, that sort of relationship is probably not something you really see in other countries.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) When そういう, こういう and ああいう refer to something/someone the speaker sees or perceives, they are used for something/someone close to the hearer, close to the speaker, and away from both the speaker and the hearer respectively. (2) These phrases are also used to refer to something/someone the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned. Specifically, そういう is used when the speaker has just mentioned something/someone. こういう is used when the speaker has just stated something factual about something/someone. And ああいう is used when the information the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned is known to both. --- 英訳 [English translation]: that/this kind of; such --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {そう/こう/ああ}いうN
スミスさんは 昼[ひる]は 大学[だいがく]で 勉強[べんきょう] し、 夜[よる]は 病院[びょういん]で 掃除[そうじ]の アルバイトを 為[し]ている。
Smith studies at college during the day and does part-time janitorial work at a hospital at night.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The masu stem of a verb and the stem of an i-adjective + く indicate that the sentence is continuing. That is, they function like the English sentence connector "and." This use is generally restricted to written language. In spoken language the te-form of a verb or an i-adjective is commonly used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: and --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-masu、 ~ A-stem + く、 ~
日本[にほん]では、 12[じゅうに] 世紀[せいき]から 19[じゅうきゅう] 世紀[せいき]に 至[いた]るまで、 武士[ぶし]が 活躍[かつやく] した。
Samurai were active in Japan from the 12th century all the way through the 19th century.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 から N2 に至まで "from N1 all the way through N2; from N1 to even N2." This construction indicates a span of time or space and emphasizes the size of that span at the same time. It can also be used for other than spatial or temporal spans, as seen here. Primarily used in written language.
私[わたし]と 弟[おとうと]は 都市[とし]は 3[さん]歳[さい] 違[ちが]うが、 同[おな]じ 日[ひ]に 生[う]まれたので、 今日[きょう]は 私[わたし]の 誕生[たんじょう] 日[び]でも あり、 弟[おとうと]の 誕生[たんじょう] 日[び]でも ある。
My brother's three years younger than I am, but we were born on the same date, so today is both his birthday and mine.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N／ANa でもある "be also" X は Y でもある. OR X は Y でもあり、Z でもある。 Are used to introduce another property of X when X has more than one property.
昨日[きのう]、 弟[おとうと]の 友達[ともだち]が たくさん 来[き]ていたから、 この ゲームを 壊[こわ]したのは、 弟[おとうと]達[たち]に 違[ちが]い ない。
My younger brother had a lot of friends over yesterday, so I'm sure they were the ones who broke the game
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure indicates that the speaker is certain that something is true or is the case. It is used primarily in written language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: must; I'm sure/certain that ~; It is certain that ~; I'm certain that ~; be sure to V. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜に違いない
背[せ]が 高[たか]いのは 弟[おとうと]の 方[ほう]だ。でも、 足[あし]が 速[はや]いのは 僕[ぼく]の 方[ほう]だ。
It is my younger brother who is tall. But it is I who am faster.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
説明 [explanation]: The structure SのはXの方だ is used to emphasize that it is X that makes the proposition in S true. --- 英訳 [English translation]: It is X that S --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ SのはXの方だ。
剣道[けんどう]は とても 日本[にほん]らしい スポーツだと 思[おも]う。
Kendo is a sport that represents the essence of Japan.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N らしい means that something/someone is representative of N. and XはNらしい conveys the idea that X has the positive characteristics of N. NOTE: らしい is an i-adjective so the noun-mod and adverbial forms are らしい and らしく respectively.
試験[しけん]の ために 徹夜[てつや]を する つもりで コーヒーを たくさん 飲[の]んだ。 ところが、 すぐ 寝[ね]てしまった。
I drank lots of coffee, thinking I would stay up all night studying for the test, but I ended up falling asleep immediately.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ところが is a sentence initial conjunction used when something takes place which is unexpected from the preceding context. The sentence after ところが represents an event or action the speaker cannot control. --- 英訳 [English translation]: however; but; nevertheless --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S１。ところが S２ where S1=what's expected; S2= what actually occurred.
姫路[ひめじ]城[じょう]は 日本[にほん]で 最[もっと]も 美[うつく]しい お城[しろ]の 一[ひと]つと して 知[し]られています。
Himejijyou castle is known as one of Japan's most beautiful castles.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: として is used to indicate the role, capacity, or occupation of someone or the function or characteristics of something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: as; in the capacity of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nとして
父[ちち]は 家族[かぞく]の ために 一生[いっしょう] 懸命[けんめい] 働[はたら]いている。
Father works his hardest for the sake of his family.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by a noun or the non-past form of a verb, it indicates either purpose or reason/cause. In different contexts, Noun のため(に) also indicates benefit, as seen in the example sentence in this flashcard. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in order to; to; for the purpose of; for; for the sake of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nのため(に) N1のためのN2 Verb plainため(に) Verb plainためのN
一生[いっしょう] 懸命[けんめい] 勉強[べんきょう] したら、 日本[にほん]語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]になったばかりでなく、 成績[せいせき]も よくなった。
I studied as hard as I could, and not only did I get better at Japanese, but my grades also improved.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1(part) ばかりでなく N2(part) +(も） This structure is similar to XだけでなくY(も). It is usually used in written language.
一生[いっしょう] 懸命[けんめい]に 就職[しゅうしょく] 活動[かつどう]を したが、 日本[にほん]の 会社[かいしゃ]に 就職[しゅうしょく] できなかった。 そこで、 だいがく いんに すすむ ことに した。
I worked my hardest to hunt for a job, but I wasn't able to get a job at a Japanese company, so I decided to continue on to graduate school.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1, そこで, S2. "Because of that; therefore; so" そこで is used to indicate and action (to be) taken because of the situation presented in S1. それで may replace そこで そこで may only replace それで when S2 is a controllable action. ex. 寒かった。それで、見に来た人が少なかった。 only それで can be used here.
子供[こども]の 時[とき]、 ピアノを 一生[いっしょう] 懸命[けんめい]に 練習[れんしゅう] したけど、 思[おも]う ように 引[ひ]けなかったので、 辞[や]めてしまった。
When I was young I practiced piano as hard as I could, but I wasn't able to play as well as I wanted, so I ended up quitting.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

思うように〜ない [->typically, ~ is V-potential] "not ~ as one wishes" This phrase means that something is not in accord with the speaker's/writer's (or the subject's) wish or desire. The verb potential form is usually used in this structure.)
大学[だいがく]で 一生[いっしょう] 懸命[けんめい] 勉強[べんきょう] するのは いい ことです。 しかしながら、 宿題[しゅくだい]や 研究[けんきゅう]ばかりで、 友達[ともだち]も できないのは よく ありません。
It's a good thing to study hard in college. It's not good, however, to spend all your time with homework and research and not make any friends.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S1. しかしながら S2. "however, but" しかしながら is a disjunctive conjunction and appears only in sentence-initial position. It is a highly formal expression and is used typically in written language.
税金[ぜいきん]を 払[はら]う ことは、 国民[こくみん]の 句[く]に 対[たい]する 義務[ぎむ]である。
Paying taxes is a citizen's responsibility to his country.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 に対する N2 "toward; for; in; with regard to" This grammar marks something to/toward/about which one does something, or mark someone to/toward whom one does something or owes something. In different contexts, it can mark something one has interest in. Do not confuse with the use where に対して indicates two contrasting actions, states, situations, etc."toward; for; in; with regard to" This grammar marks something to/toward/about which one does something, or mark someone to/toward whom one does something or owes something. In different contexts, it can mark something one has interest in. Do not confuse with the use where に対して indicates two contrasting actions, states, situations, etc.
日本[にほん]人[じん]は 一般[いっぱん]的[てき]に 丁寧[ていねい]だと 思[おも]われている。
It is believed that the Japanese are generally polite.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: S と考えられている and S と思われている is used to introduce a generally-accepted opinion regarding some matter. 考えられている usually indicates an opinion arrived at through logic, and 思われている usually indicates an opinion derived from intuition. Note that S と考えられている and S と思われている indicates the speaker/writer's opinion. --- 英訳 [English translation]: It is believed that~; It is considered that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S-plain と{考えられている/思われている}
日本[にほん]人[じん]は 丁寧[ていねい]で 親切[しんせつ]だ。 そう いう 話[はなし]を よく 聞[き]く。
The Japanese are polite and kind. I often hear that kind of story.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) When そういう, こういう and ああいう refer to something/someone the speaker sees or perceives, they are used for something/someone close to the hearer, close to the speaker, and away from both the speaker and the hearer respectively. (2) These phrases are also used to refer to something/someone the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned. Specifically, そういう is used when the speaker has just mentioned something/someone. こういう is used when the speaker has just stated something factual about something/someone. And ああいう is used when the information the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned is known to both. --- 英訳 [English translation]: that/this kind of; such --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {そう/こう/ああ}いうN
漢字[かんじ]を 覚[おぼ]える 時[とき]は、 フラッシュ カードを 作[つく]るとか、 何[なん]回[かい]も 書[か]くとか 為[な]るといいです。
When trying to memorize kanji, making flashcards and writing them over and over is good to do.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: とか is used to list examples non-exhaustively. It is similar to や in meaning when the examples listed are nouns. Unlike や, however, とか can be preceeded by verb phrases (like in this example).. When two or more items are listed, とか after the final item is optional when it is followed by a particle and mandatory otherwise. (Note that や does not occur after the final item). In Subject とか Subject とかする, the final とか is not optional. --- 英訳 [English translation]: things/places/etc. like ~; and; or --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Noun とか Noun (とか) b. Sentence-plain とか Sentence-plain とか {する/できる}
僕[ぼく]に とって、 忘[わす]れない 場所[ばしょ]は、 彼女[かのじょ]と 初[はじ]めて 会[あ]った 喫茶[きっさ]店[てん]です。
One place that I'll never forget is the café where I first met my girlfriend.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Xにとって means "to X; for X" in a context where something (or someone) is important to X, or is necessary, useful, good, difficult, etc. for X. X is often a person, a geographic unit or an organization. --- 英訳 [English translation]: for, to, from the standpoint of, as far as ... is concerned --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nに取って
この 豆腐[とうふ]、 古[ふる] そうだよ。 いつ 買[か]ったんだっけ？
This tofu looks old. When did we buy it?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{V/A}-plain.past (んだ）っけ っけ is a question marker used in very casual conversation. Note that after the non-past forms of V, A and ~ない, んだ must be used before っけ。
昨日[きのう]は 久[ひさ]しぶりに 会[あ]った 友達[ともだち]と 一[いち] 晩[ばん]中[じゅう] 話[はな]し込[こ]んで、 徹夜[てつや] してしまった。
Yesterday, I got deep into conversation with a friend I hadn't seen in a while and ended up pulling an all-nighter.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V−masu 込む "in; into; deeply; heavily; thoroughly; completely" The compound verb base 込む can mean one of 4 things: (c) being heavily involved in something {話し込む}
どの 国[くに]の 言葉[ことば]でも、 丁寧[ていねい]になればなる 補文[ほぶん]が 長[なが]くなると いった 傾向[けいこう]が ある。
No matter what language, the higher the level of politeness, the longer the sentence tends to become.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

Phr1(、Phr2,~)といった {N/NP} [in this structure, Phr could also be a sentence] "like; such as N" といった X is used to present examples of X. X is always a noun or noun phrase. といった may be preceded by nouns, noun phrases and sentences. * If preceded by nouns, 2+ nouns are presented ** If preceded by sentences or phrases, only one sentence or phrase is presented. などのN and のような N are similar in meaning, but they are usually not preceded by sentences.
熊[くま]は 冬眠[とうみん] する 事[こと]で 知[し]られていますが、 動物[どうぶつ]園[えん]の 熊[くま]も 冬眠[とうみん]を 為[し]ますか。
Bears are known for hibernating, but do bears in zoos hibernate, too?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
